class Codebolt {
    websocket: WebSocket | null = null;
    private isReady: boolean = false;
    private readyPromise: Promise<void>;
    private readyHandlers: Array<() => void | Promise<void>> = [];
    private messageQueue: FlatUserMessage[] = [];
    private messageResolvers: Array<(message: FlatUserMessage) => void> = [];

     * @description Initializes the websocket connection.
     */
    constructor() {
        //console.log("Codebolt Agent initialized");
        this.readyPromise = this.initializeConnection();
        this.setupMessageListener()
        this.lastUserMessage = undefined
    }

    /**
     * @method initializeConnection
     * @description Initializes the WebSocket connection asynchronously.
     * @private
     */
    private async initializeConnection(): Promise<void> {
        try {
            await cbws.initializeWebSocket();
            this.websocket = cbws.getWebsocket;
            this.isReady = true;
            //console.log("Codebolt WebSocket connection established");

            // Execute all registered ready handlers
            for (const handler of this.readyHandlers) {
                try {
                    await handler();
                } catch (error) {
                    console.error('Error executing ready handler:', error);
                }
            }
        } catch (error) {
            console.error('Failed to initialize WebSocket connection:', error);
            throw error;
        }
    }

    /**

     * @description Waits for the Codebolt instance to be fully initialized.

    async waitForReady(): Promise<void> {

    get ready(): boolean {

/**
 * @class Codebolt
 * @description This class provides a unified interface to interact with various modules.
 */
class Codebolt {
    websocket: WebSocket | null = null;
    private isReady: boolean = false;
    private readyPromise: Promise<void>;
    private readyHandlers: Array<() => void | Promise<void>> = [];
    private messageQueue: FlatUserMessage[] = [];
    private messageResolvers: Array<(message: FlatUserMessage) => void> = [];
    private lastUserMessage: FlatUserMessage | undefined

    /**
     * @constructor
     * @description Initializes the websocket connection.
     */
    constructor() {
        //console.log("Codebolt Agent initialized");
        this.readyPromise = this.initializeConnection();
        this.setupMessageListener()
        this.lastUserMessage = undefined
    }

    /**
     * @method initializeConnection
     * @description Initializes the WebSocket connection asynchronously.
     * @private
     */
    private async initializeConnection(): Promise<void> {
        try {
            await cbws.initializeWebSocket();
            this.websocket = cbws.getWebsocket;
            this.isReady = true;
            //console.log("Codebolt WebSocket connection established");

            // Execute all registered ready handlers
            for (const handler of this.readyHandlers) {
                try {
                    await handler();
                } catch (error) {
                    console.error('Error executing ready handler:', error);
                }
            }
        } catch (error) {
            console.error('Failed to initialize WebSocket connection:', error);
            throw error;
        }
    }

    /**
     * @method waitForReady
     * @description Waits for the Codebolt instance to be fully initialized.
     * @returns {Promise<void>} A promise that resolves when the instance is ready.
     */
    async waitForReady(): Promise<void> {
        return this.readyPromise;
    }

    /**
     * @method isReady
     * @description Checks if the Codebolt instance is ready for use.

    get ready(): boolean {

const TUI_RESPONSE_TYPES = {

    PRESS: 'tuiPressResponse',
    RESIZE: 'tuiResizeResponse',
    SEARCH: 'tuiSearchResponse',

    WAIT: 'tuiWaitResponse',
    WHEEL: 'tuiWheelResponse',
    SESSIONS_LIST: 'tuiSessionsListResponse',
    SESSIONS_SWITCH: 'tuiSessionsSwitchResponse',
    KILL: 'tuiKillResponse',
    CLEANUP: 'tuiCleanupResponse',
} as const;

const COMMAND_EVENT_TYPES = {
    LIST: 'terminalCommandsList',
    STOP: 'terminalCommandStop',
    OUTPUT: 'terminalCommandOutput',
    STATUS: 'terminalCommandStatus',
    WAIT: 'terminalCommandWait',
} as const;

const COMMAND_RESPONSE_TYPES = {
    LIST: 'terminalCommandsListResponse',
    STOP: 'terminalCommandStopResponse',
    OUTPUT: 'terminalCommandOutputResponse',
    STATUS: 'terminalCommandStatusResponse',
    WAIT: 'terminalCommandWaitResponse',
} as const;

/**
 * CustomEventEmitter class that extends the Node.js EventEmitter class.
 */
class CustomEventEmitter extends EventEmitter {
    cleanup?: () => void;
}
/**
 * A module for executing commands in a terminal-like environment via WebSocket.
 */
const cbterminal = {
    eventEmitter: new CustomEventEmitter(),

        type: (params: { sessionId?: string; text: string }) =>

        write: (params: { sessionId?: string; data: string }) =>
            sendTuiRequest(TUI_EVENT_TYPES.WRITE, TUI_RESPONSE_TYPES.WRITE, params),

        press: (params: { sessionId?: string; keys: string[] | string }) =>
            sendTuiRequest(TUI_EVENT_TYPES.PRESS, TUI_RESPONSE_TYPES.PRESS, params),

        resize: (params: { sessionId?: string; cols: number; rows: number }) =>
            sendTuiRequest(TUI_EVENT_TYPES.RESIZE, TUI_RESPONSE_TYPES.RESIZE, params),

        search: (params: { sessionId?: string; pattern: string; regex?: boolean }) =>

        region: (params: { sessionId?: string; row: number; col: number; rows: number; cols: number; trimWhitespace?: boolean }) =>
            sendTuiRequest(TUI_EVENT_TYPES.REGION, TUI_RESPONSE_TYPES.REGION, params),

        cursor: (params: { sessionId?: string } = {}) =>

        wheel: (params: { sessionId?: string; direction: 'up' | 'down' | 'left' | 'right'; amount?: number; row?: number; col?: number; protocol?: 'auto' | 'sgr' | 'normal' }) =>

        sessions: {

        },

        kill: (params: { sessionId?: string } = {}) =>
            sendTuiRequest(TUI_EVENT_TYPES.KILL, TUI_RESPONSE_TYPES.KILL, params),

        cleanup: (params: { exitedOnly?: boolean; all?: boolean } = {}) =>
            sendTuiRequest(TUI_EVENT_TYPES.CLEANUP, TUI_RESPONSE_TYPES.CLEANUP, params),
    },

    /**
     * Executes a given command and returns the result.
     * Listens for messages from the WebSocket that indicate the output, error, or finish state
     * of the executed command and resolves the promise accordingly.
     *
     * @param {string} command - The command to be executed.
     * @returns {Promise<CommandOutput|CommandError>} A promise that resolves with the command's output, error, or finish signal.
     */
    executeCommand: async (
        command: string,
        options: boolean | ExecuteCommandOptions = false
    ): Promise<CommandOutput | CommandError | CommandFinish | any> => {
        const normalizedOptions: ExecuteCommandOptions = typeof options === 'boolean'
            ? { returnEmptyStringOnSuccess: options }
            : options;

        return cbws.messageManager.sendAndWaitForResponse(
            {
                "type": TerminalEventType.EXECUTE_COMMAND,
                "message": command,
                returnEmptyStringOnSuccess: normalizedOptions.returnEmptyStringOnSuccess ?? false,
                executionMode: normalizedOptions.executionMode,
                yieldMs: normalizedOptions.yieldMs,
                timeoutMs: normalizedOptions.timeoutMs,
                backgroundOnYield: normalizedOptions.backgroundOnYield,
                lifetime: normalizedOptions.lifetime,
                taskKind: normalizedOptions.taskKind
            },
            TerminalResponseType.COMMAND_ERROR_OR_FINISH
        );
    },

    listCommands: () =>
        sendTuiRequest(COMMAND_EVENT_TYPES.LIST, COMMAND_RESPONSE_TYPES.LIST, {}),

    stopCommand: (processId: number) =>

    readCommandOutput: (processId: number, params: { lines?: number; tailBytes?: number } = {}) =>
        sendTuiRequest(COMMAND_EVENT_TYPES.OUTPUT, COMMAND_RESPONSE_TYPES.OUTPUT, { processId, ...params }),

    getCommandStatus: (processId: number) =>
        sendTuiRequest(COMMAND_EVENT_TYPES.STATUS, COMMAND_RESPONSE_TYPES.STATUS, { processId }),

    waitCommand: (processId: number, params: { timeoutMs?: number } = {}) =>
        sendTuiRequest(COMMAND_EVENT_TYPES.WAIT, COMMAND_RESPONSE_TYPES.WAIT, { processId, ...params }),

    /**
     * Executes a given command and keeps running until an error occurs.
     * Listens for messages from the WebSocket and resolves the promise when an error is encountered.
     *
     * @param {string} command - The command to be executed.
     * @returns {Promise<CommandError>} A promise that resolves when an error occurs during command execution.
     */
    executeCommandRunUntilError: async (command: string,executeInMain=false): Promise<CommandError> => {
        return cbws.messageManager.sendAndWaitForResponse(
            {
                "type": TerminalEventType.EXECUTE_COMMAND_RUN_UNTIL_ERROR,
                "message": command,
                executeInMain
            },

/**
 * Recursively stop all child threads and their associated agents
 * @param parentThreadId The parent thread ID whose children should be stopped
 */
const stopChildThreads = async (parentThreadId: string): Promise<void> => {
    try {
        // Get all child threads for this parent
        const childThreads = await threadFileStore.getChildThreads(parentThreadId);

        if (childThreads.length === 0) {
            logger.debug(`No child threads found for parent: ${parentThreadId}`);
            return;
        }

        logger.info(`[StopChildThreads] Found ${childThreads.length} child thread(s) to stop for parent: ${parentThreadId}`);

        for (const childThread of childThreads) {
            const childThreadId = childThread.threadId;

            try {
                // First, recursively stop any grandchild threads
                await stopChildThreads(childThreadId);

                llmService.cancelActiveRequestsForThread(childThreadId, 'child_thread_stopped');

                // Stop all agent processes associated with this child thread
                const stoppedCount = await agentProcessManager.stopProcessesByThreadId(childThreadId, false);
                logger.info(`[StopChildThreads] Stopped ${stoppedCount} process(es) for child thread: ${childThreadId}`);

                // Update child thread status to stopped when it is interrupted by its parent
                await updateThreadStatusAndNotify(
                    childThreadId,
                    'stopped',
                    'Thread stopped because parent thread stopped'
                );

                // Store THREAD_FINISHED event for observability
                chatManager.addObservabilityEvent({
                    eventId: getMessageId(),
                    eventType: 'THREAD_FINISHED',
                    threadId: childThreadId,
                    parentThreadId: parentThreadId,
                    timestamp: new Date().toISOString(),
                    metadata: { reason: 'parent_thread_stopped' }
]]></tool_result>

<message role="assistant" ordinal="415" timestamp="2026-07-06T14:31:45.786Z">
Implemented the revised lifecycle model.

What changed:
- Async tasks now use `lifetime: run_scoped | detached`; `detached` is no longer a task status.
- User force-stop now immediately stops run-scoped commands/child threads owned by that agent run.
- Explicitly detached tasks survive force-stop and are injected into the next agent context as background tasks.
- Natural completion blocks only unresolved run-scoped tasks and forces the agent to `wait`, `stop`, or `detach`.
- Command tools now expose `execution_mode`, `lifetime`, and `task_kind`.
- Thread tools now expose `lifetime`, defaulting to `run_scoped`.
- Added a fallback child-thread cleanup path that skips detached or already-final async task records.
- Added shared schema/type support for thread `lifetime`.

Key files:
- [asyncTaskRegistry.cli.ts](D:/codeboltapps/Codebolt/packages/server/src/cliLib/asyncTaskRegistry.cli.ts)
- [asyncTaskService.cli.ts](D:/codeboltapps/Codebolt/packages/server/src/cliLib/asyncTaskService.cli.ts)
- [messageService.cli.ts](D:/codeboltapps/Codebolt/packages/server/src/cliLib/messageService.cli.ts)
- [aiTerminal.ts](D:/codeboltapps/Codebolt/packages/server/src/sockets/aiTerminal.ts)
- [environmentContextModifier.ts](D:/codeboltapps/Codebolt/sdks/agent/src/processor-pieces/messageModifiers/environmentContextModifier.ts)
- [responseExecutor.ts](D:/codeboltapps/Codebolt/sdks/agent/src/unified/base/responseExecutor.ts)
- [execute-command.ts](D:/codeboltapps/Codebolt/sdks/codeboltjs/src/tools/terminal/execute-command.ts)
- [thread-create-start.ts](D:/codeboltapps/Codebolt/sdks/codeboltjs/src/tools/thread/thread-create-start.ts)

Validation:
- `npm run build --workspace=packages/server` passed.
- `npx tsc --noEmit --project packages/types/tsconfig.json` passed.
- `sdks/codeboltjs` and `sdks/agent` builds still fail on existing exported-type issues unrelated to this lifecycle change, including missing `GetRegisteredTools*`, `WaitForThreadCompletionResponse`, and `AgentLocalTool*` exports.

+    private async formatPendingAsyncTasks(): Promise<string | null> {
+        try {
+            const response = await (codebolt as any).asyncTask.listTasks({
+                scope: 'thread',
+            });
+            const tasks = Array.isArray((response as any)?.tasks) ? (response as any).tasks : [];
+            const unresolvedTasks = tasks.filter((task: any) =>
+                task &&
+                task.lifetime !== 'detached' &&
+                !['completed', 'failed', 'stopped'].includes(task.status),
+            );
+            const detachedTasks = tasks.filter((task: any) =>
+                task &&
+                task.lifetime === 'detached' &&
+                !['completed', 'failed', 'stopped'].includes(task.status),
+            );
+            if (unresolvedTasks.length === 0 && detachedTasks.length === 0) {
+                return null;
+            }
+
+            const sections: string[] = [];
+            if (unresolvedTasks.length > 0) {
+                sections.push([
+                    '<pending_async_tasks>',
+                    'These run-scoped async tasks are still unresolved for this thread. Before completing, choose wait, stop, or detach for each task using async_task_control. Detach only intentional background services that should survive agent stop.',
+                    JSON.stringify(unresolvedTasks, null, 2),
+                    '</pending_async_tasks>',
+                ].join('\n'));
+            }
+            if (detachedTasks.length > 0) {
+                sections.push([
+                    '<detached_async_tasks>',
+                    'These detached async tasks are still running in the background for this thread. They do not block completion and survive user force-stop. Stop them with async_task_control if they are no longer needed.',
+                    JSON.stringify(detachedTasks, null, 2),
+                    '</detached_async_tasks>',
+                ].join('\n'));
+            }
+
+            return sections.join('\n\n');
+        } catch (error) {
+            console.error('Error reading pending async tasks:', error);
+            return null;
+        }
+    }

import logger from '../utils/appLogger';

export type AsyncTaskType = 'thread' | 'command' | 'action_block' | 'remote_job';
export type AsyncTaskStatus = 'running' | 'completed' | 'failed' | 'stopped';
export type AsyncTaskLifetime = 'run_scoped' | 'detached';
export type AsyncTaskExecutionMode = 'foreground' | 'auto' | 'background';
export type AsyncTaskKind = 'finite' | 'long_running' | 'unknown';
export type AsyncTaskScope = 'current_run' | 'thread' | 'all';

export interface AsyncTaskRecord {
    taskId: string;
    type: AsyncTaskType;
    status: AsyncTaskStatus;
    lifetime: AsyncTaskLifetime;
    executionMode?: AsyncTaskExecutionMode;
    taskKind?: AsyncTaskKind;
    ownerThreadId?: string;
    ownerAgentId?: string;
    ownerAgentInstanceId?: string;
    startedAt: string;
    updatedAt: string;
    endedAt?: string;
    title?: string;
    summary?: string;
    metadata?: Record<string, any>;
}

export interface AsyncTaskListInput {
    scope?: AsyncTaskScope;
    threadId?: string;
    agentId?: string;
    agentInstanceId?: string;
    includeCompleted?: boolean;
}

export interface AsyncTaskRegisterInput {
    taskId: string;
    type: AsyncTaskType;
    ownerThreadId?: string;
    ownerAgentId?: string;
    ownerAgentInstanceId?: string;
    title?: string;
    summary?: string;
    lifetime?: AsyncTaskLifetime;
    executionMode?: AsyncTaskExecutionMode;
    taskKind?: AsyncTaskKind;
    metadata?: Record<string, any>;
}

type AsyncTaskWaiter = {
    resolve: (record: AsyncTaskRecord) => void;
    timeoutId?: NodeJS.Timeout;
};

const FINAL_STATUSES = new Set<AsyncTaskStatus>(['completed', 'failed', 'stopped']);
const MAX_TASKS = 500;

function nowIso(): string {
    return new Date().toISOString();
}

class AsyncTaskRegistry {
    private readonly tasks = new Map<string, AsyncTaskRecord>();
    private readonly waiters = new Map<string, AsyncTaskWaiter[]>();

    registerTask(input: AsyncTaskRegisterInput): AsyncTaskRecord {
        const timestamp = nowIso();
        const existing = this.tasks.get(input.taskId);
        const record: AsyncTaskRecord = {
            ...(existing || {}),
            taskId: input.taskId,
            type: input.type,
            status: existing?.status && !FINAL_STATUSES.has(existing.status) ? existing.status : 'running',
            lifetime: input.lifetime || existing?.lifetime || 'run_scoped',
            executionMode: input.executionMode || existing?.executionMode,
            taskKind: input.taskKind || existing?.taskKind || 'unknown',
            ownerThreadId: input.ownerThreadId || existing?.ownerThreadId,
            ownerAgentId: input.ownerAgentId || existing?.ownerAgentId,
            ownerAgentInstanceId: input.ownerAgentInstanceId || existing?.ownerAgentInstanceId,
            startedAt: existing?.startedAt || timestamp,
            updatedAt: timestamp,
            title: input.title || existing?.title,
            summary: input.summary || existing?.summary,
            metadata: {
                ...(existing?.metadata || {}),
                ...(input.metadata || {}),
            },
        };

        this.tasks.set(input.taskId, record);
        this.prune();
        return { ...record };
    }

    updateTask(taskId: string, updates: Partial<AsyncTaskRecord>): AsyncTaskRecord | undefined {
        const existing = this.tasks.get(taskId);
        if (!existing) {
            return undefined;
        }

        const timestamp = nowIso();
        const status = updates.status || existing.status;
        const record: AsyncTaskRecord = {
            ...existing,
            ...updates,
            metadata: {
                ...(existing.metadata || {}),
                ...(updates.metadata || {}),
            },
            updatedAt: timestamp,
            endedAt: FINAL_STATUSES.has(status) ? updates.endedAt || existing.endedAt || timestamp : updates.endedAt || existing.endedAt,
        };

        this.tasks.set(taskId, record);
        if (FINAL_STATUSES.has(record.status)) {
            this.resolveWaiters(record);
        }
        return { ...record };
    }

    getTask(taskId: string): AsyncTaskRecord | undefined {
        const record = this.tasks.get(taskId);
        return record ? { ...record } : undefined;
    }

    listTasks(input: AsyncTaskListInput = {}): AsyncTaskRecord[] {
        const scope = input.scope || 'thread';
        return Array.from(this.tasks.values())
            .filter(task => input.includeCompleted || !FINAL_STATUSES.has(task.status))
            .filter(task => {
                if (scope === 'all') {
                    return true;
                }
                if (scope === 'current_run') {
                    return Boolean(
                        (!input.threadId || task.ownerThreadId === input.threadId) &&
                        (!input.agentId || task.ownerAgentId === input.agentId) &&
                        (!input.agentInstanceId || task.ownerAgentInstanceId === input.agentInstanceId),
                    );
                }
                return !input.threadId || task.ownerThreadId === input.threadId;
            })
            .sort((left, right) => right.updatedAt.localeCompare(left.updatedAt))
            .map(task => ({ ...task }));
    }

    detachTask(taskId: string, reason?: string): AsyncTaskRecord | undefined {
        return this.updateTask(taskId, {
            lifetime: 'detached',
            summary: reason || 'Task detached from the owning agent run.',
        });
    }

    waitForTask(taskId: string, timeoutMs: number): Promise<{ completed: boolean; task?: AsyncTaskRecord; error?: string }> {
        const existing = this.tasks.get(taskId);
        if (!existing) {
            return Promise.resolve({ completed: false, error: `Task ${taskId} not found` });
        }

        if (FINAL_STATUSES.has(existing.status)) {
            return Promise.resolve({ completed: true, task: { ...existing } });
        }

        return new Promise((resolve) => {
            const waiter: AsyncTaskWaiter = {
                resolve: (record) => resolve({ completed: true, task: { ...record } }),
            };

            waiter.timeoutId = setTimeout(() => {
                const waiters = this.waiters.get(taskId) || [];
                this.waiters.set(taskId, waiters.filter(existingWaiter => existingWaiter !== waiter));
                resolve({
                    completed: false,
                    task: this.getTask(taskId),
                    error: `Timed out waiting for task ${taskId}`,
                });
            }, timeoutMs);

            const waiters = this.waiters.get(taskId) || [];
            waiters.push(waiter);
            this.waiters.set(taskId, waiters);
        });
    }

    private resolveWaiters(record: AsyncTaskRecord): void {
        const waiters = this.waiters.get(record.taskId);
        if (!waiters?.length) {
            return;
        }

        this.waiters.delete(record.taskId);
        for (const waiter of waiters) {
            if (waiter.timeoutId) {
                clearTimeout(waiter.timeoutId);
            }
            waiter.resolve(record);
        }
    }

    private prune(): void {
        if (this.tasks.size <= MAX_TASKS) {
            return;
        }

        const completedTasks = Array.from(this.tasks.values())
            .filter(task => FINAL_STATUSES.has(task.status))
            .sort((left, right) => left.updatedAt.localeCompare(right.updatedAt));

        for (const task of completedTasks) {
            if (this.tasks.size <= MAX_TASKS) {
                return;
            }
            this.tasks.delete(task.taskId);
            logger.debug(`[AsyncTaskRegistry] Pruned task ${task.taskId}`);
        }
    }
}

export const asyncTaskRegistry = new AsyncTaskRegistry();
export { FINAL_STATUSES as FINAL_ASYNC_TASK_STATUSES };
]]></tool_result>

    title?: string;
    summary?: string;
    lifetime?: AsyncTaskLifetime;
    executionMode?: AsyncTaskExecutionMode;
    taskKind?: AsyncTaskKind;
    metadata?: Record<string, any>;
}

type AsyncTaskWaiter = {
    resolve: (record: AsyncTaskRecord) => void;
    timeoutId?: NodeJS.Timeout;
};

const FINAL_STATUSES = new Set<AsyncTaskStatus>(['completed', 'failed', 'stopped']);
const MAX_TASKS = 500;

function nowIso(): string {
    return new Date().toISOString();
}

class AsyncTaskRegistry {
    private readonly tasks = new Map<string, AsyncTaskRecord>();
    private readonly waiters = new Map<string, AsyncTaskWaiter[]>();

    registerTask(input: AsyncTaskRegisterInput): AsyncTaskRecord {
        const timestamp = nowIso();
        const existing = this.tasks.get(input.taskId);
        const record: AsyncTaskRecord = {
            ...(existing || {}),
            taskId: input.taskId,
            type: input.type,
            status: existing?.status && !FINAL_STATUSES.has(existing.status) ? existing.status : 'running',
            lifetime: input.lifetime || existing?.lifetime || 'run_scoped',
            executionMode: input.executionMode || existing?.executionMode,
            taskKind: input.taskKind || existing?.taskKind || 'unknown',
            ownerThreadId: input.ownerThreadId || existing?.ownerThreadId,
            ownerAgentId: input.ownerAgentId || existing?.ownerAgentId,
            ownerAgentInstanceId: input.ownerAgentInstanceId || existing?.ownerAgentInstanceId,
            startedAt: existing?.startedAt || timestamp,
            updatedAt: timestamp,
            title: input.title || existing?.title,
            summary: input.summary || existing?.summary,
            metadata: {
                ...(existing?.metadata || {}),
                ...(input.metadata || {}),
            },
        };

        this.tasks.set(input.taskId, record);
        this.prune();
        return { ...record };
    }

    updateTask(taskId: string, updates: Partial<AsyncTaskRecord>): AsyncTaskRecord | undefined {
        const existing = this.tasks.get(taskId);
        if (!existing) {
            return undefined;
        }

        const timestamp = nowIso();
        const status = updates.status || existing.status;
        const record: AsyncTaskRecord = {
            ...existing,
            ...updates,
            metadata: {
                ...(existing.metadata || {}),
                ...(updates.metadata || {}),
            },
            updatedAt: timestamp,
            endedAt: FINAL_STATUSES.has(status) ? updates.endedAt || existing.endedAt || timestamp : updates.endedAt || existing.endedAt,
        };

        this.tasks.set(taskId, record);
        if (FINAL_STATUSES.has(record.status)) {
            this.resolveWaiters(record);
        }
        return { ...record };
    }

    getTask(taskId: string): AsyncTaskRecord | undefined {
        const record = this.tasks.get(taskId);
        return record ? { ...record } : undefined;
    }

    listTasks(input: AsyncTaskListInput = {}): AsyncTaskRecord[] {
        const scope = input.scope || 'thread';
        return Array.from(this.tasks.values())
            .filter(task => input.includeCompleted || !FINAL_STATUSES.has(task.status))
            .filter(task => {
                if (scope === 'all') {
                    return true;
                }
                if (scope === 'current_run') {
                    return Boolean(
                        (!input.threadId || task.ownerThreadId === input.threadId) &&
                        (!input.agentId || task.ownerAgentId === input.agentId) &&
                        (!input.agentInstanceId || task.ownerAgentInstanceId === input.agentInstanceId),
                    );
                }
                return !input.threadId || task.ownerThreadId === input.threadId;
            })
            .sort((left, right) => right.updatedAt.localeCompare(left.updatedAt))
            .map(task => ({ ...task }));
    }

    detachTask(taskId: string, reason?: string): AsyncTaskRecord | undefined {
        return this.updateTask(taskId, {
            lifetime: 'detached',
            summary: reason || 'Task detached from the owning agent run.',
        });
    }

    waitForTask(taskId: string, timeoutMs: number): Promise<{ completed: boolean; task?: AsyncTaskRecord; error?: string }> {
        const existing = this.tasks.get(taskId);
        if (!existing) {
            return Promise.resolve({ completed: false, error: `Task ${taskId} not found` });
        }

        if (FINAL_STATUSES.has(existing.status)) {
            return Promise.resolve({ completed: true, task: { ...existing } });
        }

        return new Promise((resolve) => {
            const waiter: AsyncTaskWaiter = {
                resolve: (record) => resolve({ completed: true, task: { ...record } }),
            };

            waiter.timeoutId = setTimeout(() => {
                const waiters = this.waiters.get(taskId) || [];
                this.waiters.set(taskId, waiters.filter(existingWaiter => existingWaiter !== waiter));
                resolve({
                    completed: false,
                    task: this.getTask(taskId),
                    error: `Timed out waiting for task ${taskId}`,
                });
            }, timeoutMs);

            const waiters = this.waiters.get(taskId) || [];
            waiters.push(waiter);
            this.waiters.set(taskId, waiters);
        });
    }

    private resolveWaiters(record: AsyncTaskRecord): void {
        const waiters = this.waiters.get(record.taskId);
        if (!waiters?.length) {
            return;
        }

        this.waiters.delete(record.taskId);
        for (const waiter of waiters) {
            if (waiter.timeoutId) {
                clearTimeout(waiter.timeoutId);
            }
            waiter.resolve(record);
        }
    }

    private prune(): void {
        if (this.tasks.size <= MAX_TASKS) {
            return;
        }

        const completedTasks = Array.from(this.tasks.values())
            .filter(task => FINAL_STATUSES.has(task.status))
            .sort((left, right) => left.updatedAt.localeCompare(right.updatedAt));

        for (const task of completedTasks) {
            if (this.tasks.size <= MAX_TASKS) {
                return;
            }
            this.tasks.delete(task.taskId);
            logger.debug(`[AsyncTaskRegistry] Pruned task ${task.taskId}`);
        }
    }
}

export const asyncTaskRegistry = new AsyncTaskRegistry();
export { FINAL_STATUSES as FINAL_ASYNC_TASK_STATUSES };

import agentProcessManager from '../managers/AgentProcessManager';
import { threadFileStore } from '../stores/threadFileStore';
import { stopCommandProcess, waitCommandProcess, readCommandProcessOutput } from '../sockets/aiTerminal';
import { asyncTaskRegistry, AsyncTaskRecord, AsyncTaskScope } from './asyncTaskRegistry.cli';

const DEFAULT_WAIT_TIMEOUT_MS = 30 * 1000;
const MAX_WAIT_TIMEOUT_MS = 5 * 60 * 1000;

type AsyncTaskAction = 'wait' | 'stop' | 'detach';

function normalizeTimeoutMs(value: unknown): number {
    if (typeof value !== 'number' || !Number.isFinite(value) || value < 0) {
        return DEFAULT_WAIT_TIMEOUT_MS;
    }
    return Math.min(Math.floor(value), MAX_WAIT_TIMEOUT_MS);
}

function inferTaskParts(taskId: string): { type?: string; resourceId?: string } {
    const separatorIndex = taskId.indexOf(':');
    if (separatorIndex === -1) {
        return {};
    }
    return {
        type: taskId.slice(0, separatorIndex),
        resourceId: taskId.slice(separatorIndex + 1),
    };
}

function formatResponse(type: string, success: boolean, data: Record<string, any>, error?: string) {
    return {
        type,
        success,
        ...data,
        error,
        timestamp: new Date().toISOString(),
    };
}

async function stopThreadTask(task: AsyncTaskRecord) {
    const threadId = task.metadata?.threadId || inferTaskParts(task.taskId).resourceId;
    if (!threadId) {
        return { success: false, error: `Cannot infer thread id for task ${task.taskId}` };
    }

    const stoppedCount = await agentProcessManager.stopProcessesByThreadId(threadId, false);
    await threadFileStore.updateThreadStatusSimple(threadId, 'stopped');
    asyncTaskRegistry.updateTask(task.taskId, {
        status: 'stopped',
        summary: `Stopped thread task ${threadId}`,
        metadata: { stoppedCount },
    });

    return { success: true, stoppedCount };
}

async function stopCommandTask(task: AsyncTaskRecord) {
    const processId = Number(task.metadata?.processId || inferTaskParts(task.taskId).resourceId);
    const result = stopCommandProcess(processId);
    if (!result.success) {
        return result;
    }

    asyncTaskRegistry.updateTask(task.taskId, {
        status: 'stopped',
        summary: `Stopped command process ${processId}`,
    });
    return result;
}

async function waitCommandTask(task: AsyncTaskRecord, timeoutMs: number) {
    const processId = Number(task.metadata?.processId || inferTaskParts(task.taskId).resourceId);
    const result = await waitCommandProcess(processId, { timeoutMs });

    if (result.process) {
        const status = result.process.status === 'done'
            ? 'completed'
            : result.process.status === 'failed'
                ? 'failed'
                : result.process.status === 'stopped'
                    ? 'stopped'
                    : task.status;
        asyncTaskRegistry.updateTask(task.taskId, {
            status,
            summary: result.error || task.summary,
            metadata: { commandRecord: result.process },
        });
    }

    const output = readCommandProcessOutput(processId, { lines: 80, tailBytes: 64 * 1024 });
    return {
        completed: result.success,
        task: asyncTaskRegistry.getTask(task.taskId),
        output: output.output,
        error: result.error,
    };
}

export const asyncTaskServiceCLI = {
    listTasks(params: any, finalMessage: any) {
        const scope = (params?.scope || 'thread') as AsyncTaskScope;
        const tasks = asyncTaskRegistry.listTasks({
            scope,
            threadId: params?.threadId || params?.thread_id || finalMessage?.threadId,
            agentId: params?.agentId || params?.agent_id || finalMessage?.agentId,
            agentInstanceId: params?.agentInstanceId || params?.agent_instance_id || finalMessage?.agentInstanceId,
            includeCompleted: params?.includeCompleted ?? params?.include_completed,
        });

        return formatResponse('asyncTask.listResponse', true, {
            tasks,
            output: JSON.stringify(tasks, null, 2),
        });
    },

    async controlTask(params: any, _finalMessage: any) {
        const taskId = params?.taskId || params?.task_id;
        const action = params?.action as AsyncTaskAction;
        if (!taskId || typeof taskId !== 'string') {
            return formatResponse('asyncTask.controlResponse', false, { taskId: taskId || '' }, 'Missing required parameter: taskId');
        }
        if (!['wait', 'stop', 'detach'].includes(action)) {
            return formatResponse('asyncTask.controlResponse', false, { taskId }, 'Invalid action. Expected wait, stop, or detach.');
        }

        const task = asyncTaskRegistry.getTask(taskId);
        if (!task) {
            return formatResponse('asyncTask.controlResponse', false, { taskId }, `Task ${taskId} not found`);
        }

        if (action === 'detach') {
            const detached = asyncTaskRegistry.detachTask(taskId, params?.reason);
            return formatResponse('asyncTask.controlResponse', true, {
                taskId,
                action,
                task: detached,
                output: JSON.stringify(detached, null, 2),
            });
        }

        if (action === 'stop') {
            const result = task.type === 'command'
                ? await stopCommandTask(task)
                : task.type === 'thread'
                    ? await stopThreadTask(task)
                    : { success: false, error: `Stop is not implemented for task type ${task.type}` };

            return formatResponse('asyncTask.controlResponse', Boolean(result.success), {
                taskId,
                action,
                task: asyncTaskRegistry.getTask(taskId),
                result,
                output: JSON.stringify(result, null, 2),
            }, result.success ? undefined : result.error);
        }

        const timeoutMs = normalizeTimeoutMs(params?.timeoutMs ?? params?.timeout_ms);
        const waitResult: any = task.type === 'command'
            ? await waitCommandTask(task, timeoutMs)
            : await asyncTaskRegistry.waitForTask(taskId, timeoutMs);

        return formatResponse('asyncTask.controlResponse', true, {
            taskId,
            action,
            completed: waitResult.completed,
            task: waitResult.task,
            output: waitResult.output || JSON.stringify(waitResult.task, null, 2),
            waitTimedOut: !waitResult.completed,
        }, waitResult.completed ? undefined : waitResult.error);
    },

    async handleAsyncTaskOperation(operation: string, params: any, finalMessage: any) {
        const action = operation.replace(/^asyncTask\./, '');
        if (action === 'list' || action === 'listTasks') {
            return this.listTasks(params, finalMessage);
        }
        if (action === 'control' || action === 'controlTask') {
            return this.controlTask(params, finalMessage);
        }
        return formatResponse('asyncTask.errorResponse', false, {}, `Unknown async task operation: ${operation}`);
    },

    async stopRunScopedTasksForRun(params: {
        threadId?: string;
        agentId?: string;
        agentInstanceId?: string;
    }) {
        const tasks = asyncTaskRegistry.listTasks({
            scope: 'current_run',
            threadId: params.threadId,
            agentId: params.agentId,
            agentInstanceId: params.agentInstanceId,
            includeCompleted: false,
        }).filter(task =>
            task.lifetime !== 'detached' &&
            !['completed', 'failed', 'stopped'].includes(task.status),
        );

        const stoppedTasks: any[] = [];
        const failedTasks: any[] = [];
        for (const task of tasks) {
            const result = task.type === 'command'
                ? await stopCommandTask(task)
                : task.type === 'thread'
                    ? await stopThreadTask(task)
                    : { success: false, error: `Stop is not implemented for task type ${task.type}` };

            if (result.success) {
                stoppedTasks.push({ taskId: task.taskId, type: task.type, title: task.title, result });
            } else {
                failedTasks.push({ taskId: task.taskId, type: task.type, title: task.title, result });
            }
        }

        return {
            stoppedTasks,
            failedTasks,
            detachedTasks: asyncTaskRegistry.listTasks({
                scope: 'current_run',
                threadId: params.threadId,
                agentId: params.agentId,
                agentInstanceId: params.agentInstanceId,
                includeCompleted: false,
            }).filter(task => task.lifetime === 'detached'),
        };
    },
};

import cbws from '../core/websocket';
import { randomUUID } from 'crypto';

export type AsyncTaskScope = 'current_run' | 'thread' | 'all';
export type AsyncTaskControlAction = 'wait' | 'stop' | 'detach';

export interface AsyncTaskListOptions {
    scope?: AsyncTaskScope;
    threadId?: string;
    agentId?: string;
    agentInstanceId?: string;
    includeCompleted?: boolean;
}

export interface AsyncTaskControlOptions {
    taskId: string;
    action: AsyncTaskControlAction;
    timeoutMs?: number;
    reason?: string;
}

function sendAsyncTaskRequest<T>(action: string, params: Record<string, unknown>): Promise<T> {
    const requestId = randomUUID();
    return cbws.messageManager.sendAndWaitForResponse<T>(
        {
            type: `asyncTask.${action}`,
            action,
            requestId,
            params,
        },
        `asyncTask.${action}Response`,
    );
}

const asyncTask = {
    listTasks: (options: AsyncTaskListOptions = {}) =>
        sendAsyncTaskRequest<any>('list', options as unknown as Record<string, unknown>),

    controlTask: (options: AsyncTaskControlOptions) =>
        sendAsyncTaskRequest<any>('control', options as unknown as Record<string, unknown>),
};

export default asyncTask;
]]></tool_result>

import type { ToolInvocation, ToolResult } from '../types';
import { Kind, ToolErrorType } from '../types';
import { BaseDeclarativeTool, BaseToolInvocation } from '../base-tool';
import asyncTask, { AsyncTaskScope } from '../../modules/asyncTask';

export interface AsyncTaskListParams {
    scope?: AsyncTaskScope;
    threadId?: string;
    agentId?: string;
    agentInstanceId?: string;
    includeCompleted?: boolean;
}

class AsyncTaskListInvocation extends BaseToolInvocation<AsyncTaskListParams, ToolResult> {
    constructor(params: AsyncTaskListParams) {
        super(params);
    }

    async execute(): Promise<ToolResult> {
        try {
            const response = await asyncTask.listTasks(this.params);
            if (response?.success === false) {
                const errorMessage = response.error || 'Failed to list async tasks';
                return {
                    llmContent: `Async task list failed: ${errorMessage}`,
                    returnDisplay: `Error: ${errorMessage}`,
                    error: {
                        message: errorMessage,
                        type: ToolErrorType.EXECUTION_FAILED,
                    },
                };
            }

            const tasks = response?.tasks || [];
            return {
                llmContent: `Async tasks:\n${JSON.stringify(tasks, null, 2)}`,
                returnDisplay: `Listed ${tasks.length} async task(s)`,
            };
        } catch (error) {
            const errorMessage = error instanceof Error ? error.message : 'Unknown error occurred';
            return {
                llmContent: `Error listing async tasks: ${errorMessage}`,
                returnDisplay: `Error: ${errorMessage}`,
                error: {
                    message: errorMessage,
                    type: ToolErrorType.EXECUTION_FAILED,
                },
            };
        }
    }
}

export class AsyncTaskListTool extends BaseDeclarativeTool<AsyncTaskListParams, ToolResult> {
    static readonly Name = 'async_task_list';

    constructor() {
        super(
            AsyncTaskListTool.Name,
            'AsyncTaskList',
            'Lists running and recent async tasks such as background commands and child threads, including whether each task is run_scoped or detached.',
            Kind.Other,
            {
                type: 'object',
                properties: {
                    scope: {
                        type: 'string',
                        enum: ['current_run', 'thread', 'all'],
                        description: 'Task scope. Defaults to thread.',
                    },
                    threadId: { type: 'string', description: 'Optional thread ID filter.' },
                    agentId: { type: 'string', description: 'Optional agent ID filter.' },
                    agentInstanceId: { type: 'string', description: 'Optional agent instance ID filter.' },
                    includeCompleted: { type: 'boolean', description: 'Include completed, failed, and stopped tasks.' },
                },
                required: [],
            },
        );
    }

    protected createInvocation(params: AsyncTaskListParams): ToolInvocation<AsyncTaskListParams, ToolResult> {
        return new AsyncTaskListInvocation(params);
    }
}
]]></tool_result>

import type { ToolInvocation, ToolResult } from '../types';
import { Kind, ToolErrorType } from '../types';
import { BaseDeclarativeTool, BaseToolInvocation } from '../base-tool';
import asyncTask, { AsyncTaskControlAction } from '../../modules/asyncTask';

export interface AsyncTaskControlParams {
    taskId: string;
    action: AsyncTaskControlAction;
    timeoutMs?: number;
    reason?: string;
}

class AsyncTaskControlInvocation extends BaseToolInvocation<AsyncTaskControlParams, ToolResult> {
    constructor(params: AsyncTaskControlParams) {
        super(params);
    }

    async execute(): Promise<ToolResult> {
        try {
            const response = await asyncTask.controlTask(this.params);
            if (response?.success === false) {
                const errorMessage = response.error || 'Failed to control async task';
                return {
                    llmContent: `Async task ${this.params.action} failed: ${errorMessage}`,
                    returnDisplay: `Error: ${errorMessage}`,
                    error: {
                        message: errorMessage,
                        type: ToolErrorType.EXECUTION_FAILED,
                    },
                };
            }

            const task = response?.task;
            const statusLine = task?.status
                ? `Task ${this.params.taskId} status: ${task.status}`
                : `Task ${this.params.taskId} ${this.params.action} completed`;
            const waitLine = response?.waitTimedOut
                ? '\nWait timed out; the task is still running. Choose wait again, stop it, or detach it only if it is an intentional background service.'
                : '';
            const output = response?.output ? `\n\nOutput:\n${response.output}` : '';
            return {
                llmContent: `${statusLine}${waitLine}${output}`,
                returnDisplay: statusLine,
            };
        } catch (error) {
            const errorMessage = error instanceof Error ? error.message : 'Unknown error occurred';
            return {
                llmContent: `Error controlling async task: ${errorMessage}`,
                returnDisplay: `Error: ${errorMessage}`,
                error: {
                    message: errorMessage,
                    type: ToolErrorType.EXECUTION_FAILED,
                },
            };
        }
    }
}

export class AsyncTaskControlTool extends BaseDeclarativeTool<AsyncTaskControlParams, ToolResult> {
    static readonly Name = 'async_task_control';

    constructor() {
        super(
            AsyncTaskControlTool.Name,
            'AsyncTaskControl',
            'Controls an async task. Use wait with a timeout, stop to terminate, or detach to let intentional background work survive agent completion and user force-stop.',
            Kind.Execute,
            {
                type: 'object',
                properties: {
                    taskId: {
                        type: 'string',
                        description: 'Async task ID, for example command:1234 or thread:abc.',
                    },
                    action: {
                        type: 'string',
                        enum: ['wait', 'stop', 'detach'],
                        description: 'Control action to perform.',
                    },
                    timeoutMs: {
                        type: 'number',
                        description: 'Maximum wait time in milliseconds for action=wait. The runtime caps this value.',
                    },
                    reason: {
                        type: 'string',
                        description: 'Optional reason used when detaching a task. Detach only intentional background services such as dev servers.',
                    },
                },
                required: ['taskId', 'action'],
            },
        );
    }

    protected override validateToolParamValues(params: AsyncTaskControlParams): string | null {
        if (typeof params.taskId !== 'string' || !params.taskId.trim()) {
            return "'taskId' is required and must be a non-empty string";
        }
        if (!['wait', 'stop', 'detach'].includes(params.action)) {
            return "'action' must be one of: wait, stop, detach";
        }
        return null;
    }

    protected createInvocation(params: AsyncTaskControlParams): ToolInvocation<AsyncTaskControlParams, ToolResult> {
        return new AsyncTaskControlInvocation(params);
    }
}
]]></tool_result>

+<body>
+  <header>
+    <div class="inner">
+      <h1>Async Task Lifecycle Changes</h1>
+      <p class="subtitle">
+        This document explains the current changes made across the CodeBolt server, agent SDK,
+        and codeboltjs SDK to make long-running commands and child threads explicit, controllable,
+        and predictable across normal completion, user force-stop, and future continuation.
+      </p>
+    </div>
+  </header>
+
+  <main>
+    <section>
+      <h2>Executive Summary</h2>
+      <p>
+        The implementation introduces a generic async-task layer above commands and child threads.
+        The important product rule is now simple:
+      </p>
+      <div class="grid">
+        <div class="card">
+          <h3><span class="tag tag-ok">Default</span>Run-scoped work</h3>
+          <p>
+            A task with <code>lifetime: "run_scoped"</code> belongs to the current agent run.
+            It must be resolved before the agent completes naturally, and it is stopped immediately
+            when the user force-stops the agent.
+          </p>
+        </div>
+        <div class="card">
+          <h3><span class="tag tag-warn">Explicit</span>Detached work</h3>
+          <p>
+            A task with <code>lifetime: "detached"</code> is intentionally left running in the
+            background. It survives user force-stop and natural completion, and is shown again to
+            the next agent process as background context.
+          </p>
+        </div>
+      </div>
+      <div class="callout">
+        <p>
+          The implementation deliberately avoids a frozen state. If the user force-stops an agent,
+          the runtime does not wait for the model to clean up run-scoped work. The runtime kills
+          run-scoped commands and child threads immediately. Only explicitly detached work survives.
+        </p>
+      </div>
+    </section>
+
+    <section>
+      <h2>New Core Concepts</h2>
+      <table>
+        <thead>
+          <tr>
+            <th>Concept</th>
+            <th>Values</th>
+            <th>Meaning</th>
+          </tr>
+        </thead>
+        <tbody>
+          <tr>
+            <td><code>status</code></td>
+            <td><code>running</code>, <code>completed</code>, <code>failed</code>, <code>stopped</code></td>
+            <td>
+              This is only the lifecycle state. <code>detached</code> is intentionally not a status.
+            </td>
+          </tr>
+          <tr>
+            <td><code>lifetime</code></td>
+            <td><code>run_scoped</code>, <code>detached</code></td>
+            <td>
+              This decides whether a task is owned by the current agent run or intentionally survives it.
+            </td>
+          </tr>
+          <tr>
+            <td><code>executionMode</code></td>
+            <td><code>foreground</code>, <code>auto</code>, <code>background</code></td>
+            <td>
+              This controls how a command is returned to the agent. It is separate from lifetime.
+            </td>
+          </tr>
+          <tr>
+            <td><code>taskKind</code></td>
+            <td><code>finite</code>, <code>long_running</code>, <code>unknown</code></td>
+            <td>
+              This describes what the task is expected to do. For example, a build is finite and a dev server is long-running.
+            </td>
+          </tr>
+          <tr>
+            <td><code>taskId</code></td>
+            <td><code>command:&lt;pid&gt;</code>, <code>thread:&lt;threadId&gt;</code></td>
+            <td>
+              This is the stable handle used by <code>async_task_control</code> to wait, stop, or detach.
+            </td>
+          </tr>
+        </tbody>
+      </table>
+    </section>
+
+    <section>
+      <h2>Files Changed</h2>
+      <p>
+        The change spans the server runtime, thread handling, terminal handling, SDK modules, tools,
+        and agent loop guardrails.
+      </p>
+      <ul class="file-list">
+        <li>packages/server/src/cliLib/asyncTaskRegistry.cli.ts</li>
+        <li>packages/server/src/cliLib/asyncTaskService.cli.ts</li>
+        <li>packages/server/src/cliLib/index.ts</li>
+        <li>packages/server/src/cliLib/messageService.cli.ts</li>
+        <li>packages/server/src/cliLib/terminalService.cli.ts</li>
+        <li>packages/server/src/cliLib/thread/thread-service.cli.ts</li>
+        <li>packages/server/src/sockets/aiTerminal.ts</li>
+        <li>packages/types/src/codeboltjstypes/libFunctionTypes/thread.ts</li>
+        <li>packages/types/src/wstypes/agent-to-app-ws/actions/threadEventSchemas.ts</li>
+        <li>sdks/agent/src/processor-pieces/messageModifiers/environmentContextModifier.ts</li>
+        <li>sdks/agent/src/unified/base/responseExecutor.ts</li>
+        <li>sdks/codeboltjs/src/core/Codebolt.ts</li>
+        <li>sdks/codeboltjs/src/index.ts</li>
+        <li>sdks/codeboltjs/src/modules/asyncTask.ts</li>
+        <li>sdks/codeboltjs/src/modules/agentEventQueue.ts</li>
+        <li>sdks/codeboltjs/src/modules/terminal.ts</li>
+        <li>sdks/codeboltjs/src/modules/thread.ts</li>
+        <li>sdks/codeboltjs/src/tools/asyncTask/*</li>
+        <li>sdks/codeboltjs/src/tools/index.ts</li>
+        <li>sdks/codeboltjs/src/tools/terminal/execute-command.ts</li>
+        <li>sdks/codeboltjs/src/tools/thread/thread-create-background.ts</li>
+        <li>sdks/codeboltjs/src/tools/thread/thread-create-start.ts</li>
+        <li>sdks/codeboltjs/src/tools/thread/thread-wait-for-completion.ts</li>
+      </ul>
+    </section>
+
+    <section>
+      <h2>Server-Side Runtime</h2>
+      <div class="grid">
+        <div class="card">
+          <h3>Async Task Registry</h3>
+          <p>
+            <code>asyncTaskRegistry.cli.ts</code> is the in-memory registry for async work. It stores
+            task identity, owner thread, owner agent, owner agent instance, lifecycle status, lifetime,
+            execution mode, task kind, timestamps, summary, and metadata.
+          </p>
+          <p>
+            It also supports bounded waiters. When a task reaches a final status, all waiters are
+            resolved. Old completed tasks are pruned after the registry grows beyond 500 records.
+          </p>
+        </div>
+        <div class="card">
+          <h3>Async Task Service</h3>
+          <p>
+            <code>asyncTaskService.cli.ts</code> exposes the runtime operations used by the SDK:
+            <code>list</code>, <code>control</code>, and force-stop cleanup.
+          </p>
+          <p>
+            <code>control</code> accepts <code>wait</code>, <code>stop</code>, or <code>detach</code>.
+            Waits are bounded to a maximum of five minutes. Stop is implemented for command tasks
+            and thread tasks.
+          </p>
+        </div>
+      </div>
+
+      <h3>Force-Stop Cleanup</h3>
+      <p>
+        <code>stopRunScopedTasksForRun</code> lists active tasks for the current run and stops every
+        non-detached task. Detached tasks are returned separately for observability but are not stopped.
+      </p>
+      <pre><code>User force-stops agent
+  -> messageService.handleProcessStopped(...)
+  -> asyncTaskServiceCLI.stopRunScopedTasksForRun(...)
+  -> stop command:&lt;pid&gt; tasks using stopCommandProcess(...)
+  -> stop thread:&lt;threadId&gt; tasks using agentProcessManager.stopProcessesByThreadId(...)
+  -> leave lifetime="detached" tasks running
+  -> write observability metadata listing stopped, failed, and detached tasks</code></pre>
+
+      <div class="warning callout">
+        <p>
+          There is also a fallback recursive child-thread cleanup path in <code>messageService.cli.ts</code>.
+          It skips child threads whose async task is already final or explicitly detached. This preserves
+          cleanup coverage for older child threads that may not have been registered through the new registry.
+        </p>
+      </div>
+    </section>
+
+    <section>
+      <h2>Command Handling</h2>
+      <p>
+        Commands now register themselves as async tasks when they are managed by
+        <code>aiTerminal.ts</code>. The task id is <code>command:&lt;pid&gt;</code>.
+      </p>
+      <table>
+        <thead>
+          <tr>
+            <th>Command example</th>
+            <th>Recommended mode</th>
+            <th>Recommended lifetime</th>
+            <th>Expected behavior</th>
+          </tr>
+        </thead>
+        <tbody>
+          <tr>
+            <td><code>ls</code>, <code>dir</code></td>
+            <td><code>foreground</code> or <code>auto</code></td>
+            <td><code>run_scoped</code></td>
+            <td>Usually finishes quickly and returns output normally.</td>
+          </tr>
+          <tr>
+            <td><code>cp</code>, <code>npm run build</code></td>
+            <td><code>auto</code></td>
+            <td><code>run_scoped</code></td>
+            <td>
+              If it takes longer than the yield window, the agent gets <code>command:&lt;pid&gt;</code>
+              and must wait or stop before completing.
+            </td>
+          </tr>
+          <tr>
+            <td><code>npm run dev</code></td>
+            <td><code>background</code></td>
+            <td><code>detached</code></td>
+            <td>
+              Intended dev server. It can survive agent completion or user force-stop, but only if
+              explicitly started or promoted as detached.
+            </td>
+          </tr>
+        </tbody>
+      </table>
+
+      <h3>Command Task Metadata</h3>
+      <p>
+        When <code>registerManagedCommand</code> runs, it registers a task with owner thread, owner agent,
+        owner agent instance, command text, terminal id, process id, execution mode, lifetime, and task kind.
+        When the process exits, <code>finalizeManagedCommand</code> updates the async task to
+        <code>completed</code>, <code>failed</code>, or <code>stopped</code>.
+      </p>
+      <p>
+        If the command yields while still running, the registry receives yield metadata such as
+        <code>yieldReason</code>, <code>port</code>, and an output tail. If a port is detected, the task
+        kind is promoted to <code>long_running</code>.
+      </p>
+    </section>
+
+    <section>
+      <h2>Child Thread Handling</h2>
+      <p>
+        Child threads are also registered as async tasks. The task id is <code>thread:&lt;threadId&gt;</code>.
+      </p>
+      <div class="flow">
+        <div class="step">
+          <strong>Create/start</strong>
+          <span>
+            <code>thread_create_start</code> or <code>thread_create_background</code> passes
+            <code>lifetime</code> into <code>thread-service.cli.ts</code>. Default is
+            <code>run_scoped</code>.
+          </span>
+        </div>
+        <div class="step">
+          <strong>Register</strong>
+          <span>
+            <code>registerPendingThreadCompletion</code> creates <code>thread:&lt;threadId&gt;</code>
+            in the async task registry with owner information and target agent metadata.
+          </span>
+        </div>
+        <div class="step">
+          <strong>Wait</strong>
+          <span>
+            <code>thread_wait_for_completion</code> is now a compatibility wrapper over
+            <code>async_task_control</code> with action <code>wait</code>. It is bounded instead of
+            blocking indefinitely.
+          </span>
+        </div>
+        <div class="step">
+          <strong>Complete</strong>
+          <span>
+            <code>notifyThreadCompletion</code> updates the task to <code>completed</code>,
+            <code>failed</code>, or <code>stopped</code> and resolves registered waiters.
+          </span>
+        </div>
+      </div>
+
+      <div class="callout">
+        <p>
+          A child thread can now be either run-scoped or detached. Run-scoped is safer by default:
+          if the parent agent is force-stopped, the child thread is stopped too. Detached is reserved
+          for independent background work.
+        </p>
+      </div>
+    </section>
+
+    <section>
+      <h2>SDK and Tool Surface</h2>
+      <div class="grid three">
+        <div class="card">
+          <h3><code>codebolt.asyncTask</code></h3>
+          <p>
+            <code>sdks/codeboltjs/src/modules/asyncTask.ts</code> adds SDK methods:
+            <code>listTasks</code> and <code>controlTask</code>. The module is exported from
+            <code>Codebolt.ts</code> and <code>index.ts</code>.
+          </p>
+        </div>
+        <div class="card">
+          <h3><code>async_task_list</code></h3>
+          <p>
+            Lists async tasks by <code>current_run</code>, <code>thread</code>, or <code>all</code>.
+            It can include completed tasks when requested.
+          </p>
+        </div>
+        <div class="card">
+          <h3><code>async_task_control</code></h3>
+          <p>
+            Controls a task with <code>wait</code>, <code>stop</code>, or <code>detach</code>.
+            Detach is described as an explicit choice for intentional background services.
+          </p>
+        </div>
+      </div>
+
+      <h3>Terminal Tool Additions</h3>
+      <pre><code>{
+  "command": "npm run dev",
+  "execution_mode": "background",
+  "lifetime": "detached",
+  "task_kind": "long_running"
+}</code></pre>
+      <p>
+        <code>execute_command</code> now forwards <code>execution_mode</code>, <code>yield_ms</code>,
+        <code>timeout_ms</code>, <code>background_on_yield</code>, <code>lifetime</code>, and
+        <code>task_kind</code> to the terminal module.
+      </p>
+
+      <h3>Thread Tool Additions</h3>
+      <pre><code>{
+  "task": "Run the background analysis",
+  "selectedAgent": "worker-agent-id",
+  "lifetime": "run_scoped"
+}</code></pre>
+      <p>
+        <code>thread_create_start</code> and <code>thread_create_background</code> now expose
+        <code>lifetime</code>. They return the async task id and tell the agent to manage the thread
+        with <code>async_task_control</code>.
+      </p>
+    </section>
+
+    <section>
+      <h2>Agent Loop Behavior</h2>
+      <h3>At the start of a new agent process</h3>
+      <p>
+        <code>EnvironmentContextModifier</code> now injects an async-task policy into the agent context.
+        It also calls <code>codebolt.asyncTask.listTasks({ scope: "thread" })</code> and adds two possible
+        context blocks:
+      </p>
+      <ul>
+        <li>
+          <code>&lt;pending_async_tasks&gt;</code> for unresolved run-scoped tasks. These require a
+          decision before completion.
+        </li>
+        <li>
+          <code>&lt;detached_async_tasks&gt;</code> for still-running detached tasks. These do not block
+          completion, but the agent is told it can stop them if they are no longer needed.
+        </li>
+      </ul>
+
+      <h3>When the model tries to finish</h3>
+      <p>
+        <code>ResponseExecutor</code> checks <code>codebolt.asyncTask.listTasks({ scope: "current_run" })</code>
+        before accepting completion. If any non-detached task is still active, it appends an internal
+        user message:
+      </p>
+      <pre><code>&lt;async_tasks_require_decision&gt;
+You attempted to complete while run-scoped async tasks owned by this run are still unresolved.
+Before completing, use async_task_control on each task with action "wait", "stop", or "detach".
+...
+&lt;/async_tasks_require_decision&gt;</code></pre>
+      <p>
+        Then it clears the final message and continues the loop, giving the model a chance to wait,
+        stop, or detach the task.
+      </p>
+
+      <h3>When the user force-stops the agent</h3>
+      <p>
+        The runtime cleanup path runs immediately. It does not ask the model to clean up because the
+        model process is being stopped. All run-scoped async tasks owned by that run are stopped.
+        Detached tasks keep running and will be visible to the next agent.
+      </p>
+
+      <h3>When the user says continue</h3>
+      <p>
+        A new agent process is spawned for the same thread. The thread-level context stack is reused,
+        and the environment context now includes current async-task state. The new agent sees:
+      </p>
+      <ul>
+        <li>which detached background tasks are still running;</li>
+        <li>any unresolved run-scoped tasks still visible for the thread;</li>
+        <li>instructions to stop, wait, or detach tasks through <code>async_task_control</code>.</li>
+      </ul>
+      <p>
+        Because run-scoped tasks are stopped on force-stop, the continuation should not inherit hidden
+        build commands or child agents still mutating the backend unless they were explicitly detached.
+      </p>
+    </section>
+
+    <section>
+      <h2>Scenario Walkthroughs</h2>
+      <div class="grid">
+        <div class="card">
+          <h3>Finite command yields</h3>
+          <ol>
+            <li>Agent runs <code>npm run build</code> with <code>execution_mode: "auto"</code>.</li>
+            <li>The command does not finish inside the yield window.</li>
+            <li>Runtime returns <code>command:&lt;pid&gt;</code>.</li>
+            <li>Before completion, the agent must use <code>async_task_control</code> to wait or stop.</li>
+            <li>If the user force-stops, the runtime stops the process.</li>
+          </ol>
+        </div>
+        <div class="card">
+          <h3>Intentional dev server</h3>
+          <ol>
+            <li>Agent runs <code>npm run dev</code> with <code>execution_mode: "background"</code>.</li>
+            <li>Agent marks it <code>lifetime: "detached"</code>.</li>
+            <li>The task does not block completion.</li>
+            <li>If the user force-stops, the server keeps running.</li>
+            <li>The next agent sees it under <code>&lt;detached_async_tasks&gt;</code>.</li>
+          </ol>
+        </div>
+        <div class="card">
+          <h3>Child thread delegation</h3>
+          <ol>
+            <li>Agent starts a child thread. Default lifetime is <code>run_scoped</code>.</li>
+            <li>If parent completion depends on it, the agent waits using <code>async_task_control</code>.</li>
+            <li>If parent tries to complete while it is running, completion is rejected by the loop.</li>
+            <li>If user force-stops the parent, the child is stopped unless explicitly detached.</li>
+          </ol>
+        </div>
+        <div class="card">
+          <h3>User panic stop</h3>
+          <ol>
+            <li>Agent accidentally starts <code>npm run rebuild</code> and it continues running.</li>
+            <li>User force-stops the agent.</li>
+            <li>Because the command is run-scoped by default, runtime kills it immediately.</li>
+            <li>The next agent does not inherit a hidden active rebuild process.</li>
+          </ol>
+        </div>
+      </div>
+    </section>
+
+    <section>
+      <h2>What This Solves</h2>
+      <ul>
+        <li>
+          Prevents indefinite agent loops caused by long-running commands like <code>npm run dev</code>
+          when they were not explicitly detached.
+        </li>
+        <li>
+          Prevents random backend behavior after a user force-stop by killing run-scoped work immediately.
+        </li>
+        <li>
+          Gives the LLM explicit tools to wait, stop, or detach instead of making the runtime guess intent.
+        </li>
+        <li>
+          Preserves useful background services through explicit detached lifetime.
+        </li>
+        <li>
+          Makes next-turn continuity concrete by injecting detached and pending async tasks into context.
+        </li>
+      </ul>
+    </section>
+
+    <section>
+      <h2>Important Boundaries and Remaining Notes</h2>
+      <ul>
+        <li>
+          The implemented stop behavior currently handles <code>command</code> and <code>thread</code>
+          async task types. The registry type also allows <code>action_block</code> and
+          <code>remote_job</code>, but stop handling for those task types is not implemented in
+          <code>asyncTaskServiceCLI</code> yet.
+        </li>
+        <li>
+          Detached is a lifetime, not a status. A detached task can still be <code>running</code>,
+          <code>completed</code>, <code>failed</code>, or <code>stopped</code>.
+        </li>
+        <li>
+          <code>thread_wait_for_completion</code> remains available as a compatibility wrapper, but
+          the generic <code>async_task_control</code> path is the canonical control surface.
+        </li>
+        <li>
+          Validation already performed: <code>npm run build --workspace=packages/server</code> passed,
+          and <code>npx tsc --noEmit --project packages/types/tsconfig.json</code> passed. SDK builds
+          still have existing exported-type failures unrelated to this lifecycle change.
+        </li>
+      </ul>
+    </section>
+  </main>
+</body>
+</html>
*** End Patch

[async-task-lifecycle-explainer.html](D:/codeboltapps/Codebolt/async-task-lifecycle-explainer.html)

It covers:
- what changed across all modified files
- the new `status`, `lifetime`, `executionMode`, and `taskKind` model
- command and child-thread behavior
- force-stop cleanup behavior
- natural completion gate behavior

<message role="assistant" ordinal="445" timestamp="2026-07-07T06:40:10.586Z">
1. `task_kind` is barely used right now.

Current actual usage:
- It is accepted from `execute_command`.
- It is forwarded into `aiTerminal`.
- It is stored in `asyncTaskRegistry`.
- It is auto-updated to `long_running` if terminal yield detects a port.
- Child threads set `taskKind: &#34;long_running&#34;` only when detached, otherwise `unknown`.

It is not used for cleanup, completion gating, force-stop, wait, or detach decisions. So yes: currently it is mostly metadata/diagnostic, and it overlaps with things we can infer from `executionMode`, `lifetime`, and runtime observations.

I would remove `task_kind` from the LLM-facing command tool for now. If we need it later, the runtime can infer it:
- port detected -&gt; likely `long_running`
- process exits -&gt; finite/completed
- still running after yield -&gt; unknown/running
- explicitly detached -&gt; likely long-running/background service

2. I would keep `lifetime` internally, but simplify the command tool surface.

These are different concepts:

- `executionMode` = how the tool call behaves now.
  - `foreground`: wait inline.
  - `auto`: wait briefly, then return task id if still running.
  - `background`: return task id quickly.

- `lifetime` = who owns cleanup.
  - `run_scoped`: kill on user force-stop, block natural completion until resolved.
  - `detached`: survives user force-stop and natural completion.

The important case is `background + run_scoped`.

Example: `npm run build`, `npm run rebuild`, long tests, indexing, migration.
The agent may want it in background so it can inspect files or do other work while it runs, but if the user force-stops the agent, that process should be killed. So background does not automatically mean detached.

For commands, I think the clean public API should be:
<code_block language="ts"><![CDATA[
execution_mode:
  | "foreground"
  | "auto"
  | "background"
  | "detached_background"
]]></code_block>
Then derive internally:
<code_block language="ts"><![CDATA[
foreground -> executionMode=foreground, lifetime=run_scoped
auto -> executionMode=auto, lifetime=run_scoped
background -> executionMode=background, lifetime=run_scoped
detached_background -> executionMode=background, lifetime=detached
]]></code_block>
That gives the LLM one choice instead of two fields, while the runtime still keeps separate internal `executionMode` and `lifetime`.

For child threads, I would still keep `lifetime` exposed because child threads are inherently background. There the meaningful question is not foreground/auto/background; it is “should this child be owned by the parent run or detached from it?”

So my recommendation:
- Remove LLM-facing `task_kind`.
- Keep internal `taskKind` only if useful for UI/debugging, otherwise remove entirely.
- Keep internal `lifetime`.
- For command tool, replace separate `execution_mode + lifetime` with one command-facing enum: `foreground | auto | background | detached_background`.
- For child thread tools, keep `lifetime: run_scoped | detached`.
- Keep `async_task_control action=&#34;detach&#34;` because the agent may start something as run-scoped, then later decide it is intentionally background.
</message>

<message role="assistant" ordinal="447" timestamp="2026-07-07T06:55:45.508Z">
Yes, that naming is better because it makes the ownership explicit in the mode itself.

I would use this public enum:
<code_block language="ts"><![CDATA[
execution_mode:
  | "foreground_scoped"
  | "auto_scoped"
  | "background_scoped"
  | "background_detached"
]]></code_block>
Meaning:

| Mode | Runtime execution | Lifetime | Use case |
|---|---|---|---|
| `foreground_scoped` | wait inline | `run_scoped` | quick commands where agent needs output now |
| `auto_scoped` | wait briefly, yield if long | `run_scoped` | builds/tests/rebuilds that may take time |
| `background_scoped` | return task id quickly | `run_scoped` | finite background work still owned by this agent |
| `background_detached` | return task id quickly | `detached` | dev servers/watchers/services intended to survive |

Then internally we still store separate fields:
<code_block language="ts"><![CDATA[
executionMode: "foreground" | "auto" | "background"
lifetime: "run_scoped" | "detached"
]]></code_block>
Mapping:
<code_block language="ts"><![CDATA[
foreground_scoped    -> foreground + run_scoped
auto_scoped          -> auto       + run_scoped
background_scoped    -> background + run_scoped
background_detached  -> background + detached
]]></code_block>
For child threads, I agree with your direction: since child threads are inherently background, we can use only:
<code_block language="ts"><![CDATA[
execution_mode:
  | "background_scoped"
  | "background_detached"
]]></code_block>
or call it `thread_mode` if we want to avoid pretending foreground/auto apply to threads.

My preferred final shape:

For commands:
<code_block language="ts"><![CDATA[
execution_mode: "foreground_scoped" | "auto_scoped" | "background_scoped" | "background_detached"
]]></code_block>
For child threads:
<code_block language="ts"><![CDATA[
execution_mode: "background_scoped" | "background_detached"
]]></code_block>
For async task registry:
<code_block language="ts"><![CDATA[
executionMode: "foreground" | "auto" | "background"
lifetime: "run_scoped" | "detached"
]]></code_block>
And remove `task_kind` from the public tool surface. Runtime can infer long-running hints from ports, timeout/yield behavior, or detached mode.

This keeps the LLM-facing API simple, while preserving clean internal semantics.
</message>

<message role="assistant" ordinal="449" timestamp="2026-07-07T06:58:00.455Z">
Yes, we can and probably should have one common public vocabulary.

The cleanest model is:
<code_block language="ts"><![CDATA[
execution_mode:
  | "foreground_scoped"
  | "auto_scoped"
  | "background_scoped"
  | "background_detached"
]]></code_block>
Use this everywhere as the external/user-facing/task-facing mode.

Then validity depends on task type:

For commands:
<code_block language="ts"><![CDATA[
foreground_scoped
auto_scoped
background_scoped
background_detached
]]></code_block>
For child threads:
<code_block language="ts"><![CDATA[
background_scoped
background_detached
]]></code_block>
Because child threads cannot really be foreground or auto unless we implement a blocking create-and-wait mode as part of the same operation.

For async task registry, I now agree it should also store the same enum directly:
<code_block language="ts"><![CDATA[
executionMode:
  | "foreground_scoped"
  | "auto_scoped"
  | "background_scoped"
  | "background_detached"
]]></code_block>
Then we do not need a separate public/internal split.

Internally, wherever cleanup logic needs ownership, derive it:
<code_block language="ts"><![CDATA[
const isDetached = task.executionMode === "background_detached";
const isRunScoped = task.executionMode !== "background_detached";
]]></code_block>
And wherever terminal behavior needs running style, derive it:
<code_block language="ts"><![CDATA[
const shellMode =
  task.executionMode === "foreground_scoped" ? "foreground" :
  task.executionMode === "auto_scoped" ? "auto" :
  "background";
]]></code_block>
So the simpler final shape should be:
<code_block language="ts"><![CDATA[
status:
  | "running"
  | "completed"
  | "failed"
  | "stopped"

executionMode:
  | "foreground_scoped"
  | "auto_scoped"
  | "background_scoped"
  | "background_detached"
]]></code_block>
No separate `lifetime`.
No public `task_kind`.

I would still maybe keep helper functions in code:
<code_block language="ts"><![CDATA[
isDetachedExecutionMode(mode)
toShellExecutionMode(mode)
]]></code_block>
But not separate stored fields.

This is better because:
- one concept for the LLM
- one concept in the registry
- one concept in context injection
- no contradictory combinations like `foreground + detached`
- no need to explain `lifetime` separately
- child threads just accept a subset of the same enum
</message>
