function formatOutputForFileApplication(output, command, exitCode) {
    // Create a structured output format that's easy to parse
    const formattedOutput = {
        command: command,
        status: exitCode === 0 ? "success" : "error",
        exitCode: exitCode,
        timestamp: new Date().toISOString(),
        output: output.trim()
    };

    return JSON.stringify(formattedOutput, null, 2);
}

export async function executeCommandInShell(command: string, terminalId: string | number, finalMessage, notifyUser): Promise<any> {
    return new Promise(async (resolve, reject) => {
        let activeMessageId = finalMessage.messageId;
        let threadId = finalMessage.threadId;
        let initialOpenPorts: number[] = [];
        let commandCompleted = false;
        let isResolved = false;
        let resolvedAsBackground = false;
        let buffer = '';
        const executionOptions = getCommandExecutionOptions(finalMessage);
        const effectiveYieldMs = executionOptions.executionMode === 'background'
            ? (executionOptions.yieldMs ?? DEFAULT_BACKGROUND_STARTUP_CAPTURE_MS)
            : (executionOptions.yieldMs ?? DEFAULT_COMMAND_YIELD_MS);
        const MAX_BUFFER_SIZE = 512 * 1024;
        let yieldTimer: NodeJS.Timeout | undefined;
        let uiOverrideTimer: NodeJS.Timeout | undefined;
        let hardTimeoutTimer: NodeJS.Timeout | undefined;
        let timeoutId: NodeJS.Timeout | undefined;
        let intervalId: NodeJS.Timeout | undefined;

        let safeResolve = (result: any) => {
            if (!isResolved) {
                isResolved = true;
                resolve(result);
            }
        };

        let safeReject = (error: any) => {
            if (!isResolved) {
                isResolved = true;
                reject(error);
            }
        };

        const resolveAsRunning = (ptyProcess: PtyProcess, reason: string, port?: number) => {
            if (commandCompleted) return;
            resolvedAsBackground = true;
            resetTerminalIdOnProcessFinish(terminalId);
            updateTerminalProcessStatus(ptyProcess.pid, 'background');
            updateManagedCommand(ptyProcess.pid, {
                yielded: true,
                yieldReason: reason,
                port,
                outputTail: buffer.slice(-64 * 1024),
            });
            asyncTaskRegistry.updateTask(`command:${ptyProcess.pid}`, {
                ...(port ? { taskKind: 'long_running' as const } : {}),
                metadata: {
                    yieldReason: reason,
                    port,
                    outputTail: buffer.slice(-64 * 1024),
                },
            });

            const runningMessage = {
                eventType: 'console',
                type: 'command',
                message: `${command} is running in the background. View Logs.`,
                processId: ptyProcess.pid,
                command,
                status: TerminalProcessStatus.RunningInBackground,
                messageId: finalMessage.messageId,
                threadId,
                agentInstanceId: finalMessage.agentInstanceId,
                agentId: finalMessage.agentId,
                parentAgentInstanceId: finalMessage.parentAgentInstanceId,
                parentId: finalMessage.parentId,
                timestamp: new Date().toISOString(),
                port,
                reason,
            };

            if (notifyUser) updateProcessStateInUi(runningMessage);

            safeResolve({
                result: buffer || '',
                type: 'commandRunning',
                status: 'running',
                status_code: 0,
                processId: ptyProcess.pid,
                reason,
                port,
            });
        };

        // Validate command
        if (!command || command.trim() === '') {
            safeReject(new Error('Command cannot be empty'));
            return;
        }

        // Spawn a dedicated PTY for this command. Keep this guarded because
        // host bridge/native PTY load failures otherwise leave this Promise
        // pending forever when the async executor rejects.
        let ptyProcess: PtyProcess;
        try {
            ptyProcess = await spawnCommandPty(command, terminalId, finalMessage.messageId || '');
        } catch (error) {
            safeReject(error);
            return;
        }
        registerManagedCommand(ptyProcess.pid, terminalId, command, finalMessage, executionOptions);

        // Register event handlers IMMEDIATELY after spawn (before any async work)
        // to avoid race condition where fast commands exit before handlers are attached.

        // Error handling for pty process
        ptyProcess.on('error', (error) => {
            cLogger.log(FocusedLogCategory.TOOL_EXECUTION, 'error', {
                message: 'PTY process error',
                tool_name: 'terminal',
                tool_type: 'terminal',
                operation: 'execute',
                parameters: {},
                success: false,
            });
            if (!isResolved) {
                safeReject(error);
            }
        });

        // Data handler: accumulates buffer from PTY output (ANSI-stripped)
        ptyProcess.onData((ptyData: string) => {
            let data = ptyData
                .replace(/\x1b\[[0-9;]*[a-zA-Z]/g, '')
                .replace(/\x1b\][^\x07]*\x07/g, '')
                .replace(/\x1b\[\?[0-9;]*[a-zA-Z]/g, '')
                .replace(/\x1b\([A-Z]/g, '')
                .replace(/\x1b[>=]/g, '')
                .replace(/\r/g, '')
                .trim();
            if (buffer.length < MAX_BUFFER_SIZE) {
                buffer += data;
            } else if (buffer.length >= MAX_BUFFER_SIZE && !buffer.endsWith('[truncated]')) {
                buffer = buffer.slice(-MAX_BUFFER_SIZE / 2) + '\n[truncated]';
            }
        });

        // PRIMARY exit code mechanism: onExit fires when shell -c command finishes
        ptyProcess.onExit(async ({ exitCode: ptyExitCode, signal: ptySignal }) => {
            if (commandCompleted || (isResolved && !resolvedAsBackground)) return;
            const existingCommandRecord = commandRecords.get(ptyProcess.pid);
            if (existingCommandRecord && FINAL_COMMAND_STATUSES.has(existingCommandRecord.status)) return;

            logger.info(`[executeCommandInShell] PTY exited for "${command.substring(0, 50)}" exitCode=${ptyExitCode}, signal=${ptySignal}`);

            // Brief delay for remaining buffered data
            await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 200));

            if (commandCompleted || (isResolved && !resolvedAsBackground)) return;
            commandCompleted = true;

            const isPassed = ptyExitCode === 0;
            const cleanedBuffer = buffer.trim();
            const statusCode = isPassed ? 0 : (ptyExitCode ?? 1);
            const resultType = isPassed ? 'commandFinish' : 'commandError';
            const terminalStatus = isPassed ? TerminalProcessStatus.Done : TerminalProcessStatus.Failed;

            // Format output for file-related commands
            const isFileCommand = /^(cat|grep|find|ls|dir|type|echo|awk|sed|head|tail)/.test(command)
                || command.includes(" > ")
                || command.includes(" >> ");
            const formattedResult = isFileCommand
                ? formatOutputForFileApplication(cleanedBuffer, command, statusCode)
                : cleanedBuffer;

            let exitMessage = {
                eventType: 'console',
                type: 'command',
                message: isPassed ? `${command} Finished View Logs.` : `${command} Failed View Logs.`,
                processId: ptyProcess.pid,
                command,
                status: terminalStatus,
                messageId: finalMessage.messageId,
                threadId,
                agentInstanceId: finalMessage.agentInstanceId,
                agentId: finalMessage.agentId,
                parentAgentInstanceId: finalMessage.parentAgentInstanceId,
                parentId: finalMessage.parentId,
                timestamp: new Date().toISOString(),
            }

            resetTerminalIdOnProcessFinish(terminalId);
            updateTerminalProcessStatus(ptyProcess.pid, isPassed ? 'done' : 'failed');
            finalizeManagedCommand(
                ptyProcess.pid,
                isPassed ? 'done' : 'failed',
                statusCode,
                cleanedBuffer.slice(-64 * 1024),
            );
            if (notifyUser) updateProcessStateInUi(exitMessage);

            safeResolve({
                result: cleanedBuffer || '',
                formattedResult: formattedResult || '',
                type: resultType,
                status_code: statusCode,
                processId: ptyProcess.pid
            });

            // Clean up process entry and close terminal in UI
            closeLogBuffer(ptyProcess.pid);
            setTimeout(() => {
                const entry = getProcessByPid(ptyProcess.pid);
                if (entry) {
                    removeProcessFromIndexes(entry);
                    terminalProcess = terminalProcess.filter(tp => tp.ptyTerminalProcess.pid !== ptyProcess.pid);
                }
                closeTerminal(ptyProcess.pid);
            }, 1000);
        });

        let message = {
            eventType: 'console',
            type: 'command',
            message: `Executing command ${command} View Logs.`,
            processId: ptyProcess.pid,
            command,
            status: TerminalProcessStatus.Executing,
            stateEvent: 'accepted',
            messageId: activeMessageId,
            agentInstanceId: finalMessage.agentInstanceId,
            agentId: finalMessage.agentId,
            parentAgentInstanceId: finalMessage.parentAgentInstanceId,
            parentId: finalMessage.parentId,
            threadId,
            timestamp: new Date().toISOString(),
        }

        if (notifyUser) {
            subscriberToProcessStopped(message).then(async (data: any) => {
                if (commandCompleted) return;

                buffer += `User stopped the process for command : ${command}\n`;
                let stoppedMessage = {
                    eventType: 'console',
                    message: `${command} Stopped  View Logs.`,
                    processId: ptyProcess.pid,
                    type: 'command',
                    command,
                    status: TerminalProcessStatus.Stopped,
                    messageId: finalMessage.messageId,
                    agentInstanceId: finalMessage.agentInstanceId,
                    agentId: finalMessage.agentId,

function formatOutputForFileApplication(output, command, exitCode) {

        timestamp: new Date().toISOString(),
        output: output.trim()

    return JSON.stringify(formattedOutput, null, 2);

<message role="assistant" ordinal="459" timestamp="2026-07-07T07:01:23.258Z">
Yes, child threads can conceptually support all four modes if we define them consistently.

I would use one common enum everywhere:
<code_block language="ts"><![CDATA[
execution_mode:
  | "foreground_scoped"
  | "auto_scoped"
  | "background_scoped"
  | "background_detached"
]]></code_block>
Then both commands and child threads use the same vocabulary.

For child threads:

| Mode | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `foreground_scoped` | Start child thread and wait until it finishes before returning. Still owned by parent run. |
| `auto_scoped` | Start child thread, wait for a bounded time, then return `thread:&lt;id&gt;` if still running. Owned by parent run. |
| `background_scoped` | Start child thread and return task id quickly. Owned by parent run. Killed if parent/user force-stops. |
| `background_detached` | Start child thread and return task id quickly. Survives parent/user force-stop. |

That is actually cleaner. Then command and thread tools both expose the same `execution_mode`, and the implementation decides what it means for that task type.

For foreground infinite-time problem:

Current command behavior:
- `foreground` can take an optional `timeoutMs`.
- If `timeoutMs` is provided, runtime kills the command after that timeout and returns `commandError` with status code `124`.
- If no explicit `timeoutMs`, there is also an internal command-analysis timeout. When it fires, it asks LLM whether the command is `passed`, `failed`, or `processing`.
- If analysis says `processing`, or analysis fails, the command is returned as background/running instead of blocking forever.
- So current foreground is not perfectly pure foreground; the runtime has escape hatches.

Current child-thread behavior:
- `waitForThreadCompletionWithTimeout` defaults to `30s`.
- It is capped at `5 minutes`.
- If timeout happens, it returns `completed: false` and the child thread stays running as an async task.
- So child-thread “foreground” should also be bounded, not infinite.

My recommendation:

Use one field:
<code_block language="ts"><![CDATA[
execution_mode:
  | "foreground_scoped"
  | "auto_scoped"
  | "background_scoped"
  | "background_detached"
]]></code_block>
And define timeout behavior like this:
<code_block language="ts"><![CDATA[
foreground_scoped:
  Wait until completion, but still bounded by timeoutMs or runtime max.
  If timeout happens, do not leave it pretending foreground.
  Convert/return it as a running run-scoped async task.

auto_scoped:
  Wait briefly/yield window.
  If still running, return async task id.

background_scoped:
  Return async task id quickly.

background_detached:
  Return async task id quickly and mark as detached.
]]></code_block>
So foreground does not mean “can block forever”. It means “the agent wants the result inline”; runtime still must protect itself with a maximum wait.

I would remove separate `lifetime` and `task_kind`, and make `execution_mode` the single public and registry field. Internally helper functions can derive:
<code_block language="ts"><![CDATA[
isDetached = execution_mode === "background_detached"
isScoped = execution_mode !== "background_detached"
isForeground = execution_mode === "foreground_scoped"
isAuto = execution_mode === "auto_scoped"
isBackground = execution_mode === "background_scoped" || execution_mode === "background_detached"
]]></code_block>
</message>

<message role="assistant" ordinal="461" timestamp="2026-07-07T07:19:52.524Z">
Yes. That is a better model than LLM-analyzing command status.

For foreground commands, I would change behavior to:
<code_block language="text"><![CDATA[
foreground_scoped means:
  try to run inline,
  but only up to a runtime foreground timeout,
  if still running after that timeout:
    convert to background_scoped,
    return task id + logs so far,
    let the agent decide wait/stop/detach.
]]></code_block>
That makes foreground safe without guessing whether the command passed/failed/processing.

Recommended behavior:

| Mode | Initial behavior | If still running |
|---|---|---|
| `foreground_scoped` | Wait inline for longer foreground timeout | Convert to `background_scoped`, return `taskId`, logs so far |
| `auto_scoped` | Wait inline for shorter yield timeout | Convert to `background_scoped`, return `taskId`, logs so far |
| `background_scoped` | Return task id quickly | Already background scoped |
| `background_detached` | Return task id quickly | Already background detached |

So `foreground_scoped` and `auto_scoped` differ only in timeout length and intent:
- `auto_scoped`: expected to maybe continue in background, short wait.
- `foreground_scoped`: expected to finish inline, longer wait, but not infinite.

The agent can then do exactly what you said:
- call `async_task_control { action: &#34;wait&#34; }`
- wait again if needed
- stop it
- detach it if it turns out to be an intentional long-running service

I would remove the LLM command analysis path for this lifecycle decision. Runtime should not ask an LLM to classify a still-running process as passed/failed/processing. The process lifecycle is objective:
- exited with code 0 -&gt; completed
- exited nonzero -&gt; failed
- still running after timeout -&gt; background_scoped/running
- user/runtime stopped -&gt; stopped

For logs/output:
When converting foreground to background, return:
<code_block language="text"><![CDATA[
Command is still running after <timeout>ms.
It has been converted to background_scoped.

Async Task ID: command:<pid>
Status: running
Execution Mode: background_scoped

Output so far:
...
Use async_task_control with action "wait", "stop", or "detach".
]]></code_block>
One nuance: the registry should update the task’s `executionMode` from `foreground_scoped` to `background_scoped` at that point, because its behavior has changed.

So the clean final model becomes:
<code_block language="ts"><![CDATA[
status:
  "running" | "completed" | "failed" | "stopped"

executionMode:
  "foreground_scoped" | "auto_scoped" | "background_scoped" | "background_detached"
]]></code_block>
No separate `lifetime`, no public `task_kind`, no LLM command-status analysis for timeout conversion.
</message>

<message role="assistant" ordinal="463" timestamp="2026-07-07T07:21:43.015Z">
Yes. That should be generalized.

Think of it as a common task scheduler policy, not a command-specific policy:
<code_block language="ts"><![CDATA[
executionMode:
  | "foreground_scoped"
  | "auto_scoped"
  | "background_scoped"
  | "background_detached"
]]></code_block>
Common behavior for all async task types:

| Mode | Runtime behavior |
|---|---|
| `foreground_scoped` | Start task and wait inline up to a foreground timeout. If still running, convert to `background_scoped` and return task id + output/status so far. |
| `auto_scoped` | Start task and wait inline up to a shorter auto timeout. If still running, convert to `background_scoped` and return task id + output/status so far. |
| `background_scoped` | Start task and return task id quickly. Runtime owns cleanup. User force-stop kills it. Natural completion blocks until agent waits/stops/detaches. |
| `background_detached` | Start task and return task id quickly. Runtime does not kill it on user force-stop. It is shown to the next agent as detached background work. |

Then each task type implements the same small adapter contract:
<code_block language="ts"><![CDATA[
interface AsyncTaskAdapter {
  start(): Promise<TaskStartResult>;
  wait(taskId: string, timeoutMs: number): Promise<TaskWaitResult>;
  stop(taskId: string): Promise<TaskStopResult>;
  readOutput?(taskId: string): Promise<TaskOutputResult>;
}
]]></code_block>
Commands, child threads, action blocks, remote jobs can all plug into that.

Important part: timeout does not mean failure. It means:
<code_block language="text"><![CDATA[
still running -> converted/returned as background_scoped
]]></code_block>
Only actual process exit failure, thread failure, action block failure, or explicit stop should mark `failed`/`stopped`.

So for any task type:
<code_block language="text"><![CDATA[
foreground_scoped task exceeds foreground timeout
  -> status remains running
  -> executionMode becomes background_scoped
  -> agent gets taskId + latest output/status
  -> agent can wait/stop/detach

auto_scoped task exceeds auto timeout
  -> same conversion to background_scoped

background_scoped task running when agent tries to complete
  -> completion gate pushes agent to wait/stop/detach

user force-stops agent
  -> stop all background_scoped / foreground_scoped / auto_scoped tasks owned by run
  -> leave background_detached tasks running
]]></code_block>
This gives one mental model for everything. Commands are just one adapter. Child threads are another adapter. Action blocks can be added later without inventing another lifecycle.
</message>

import os from 'os';

const cLogger = CategorizedLogger.getInstance();

// Chunked PTY write to prevent node-pty buffer overflow on multiline paste.
// Writing large payloads in a single write() call can fill the PTY input buffer
// and deadlock the event loop. This breaks the payload into small chunks with
// micro-delays so the kernel can drain the buffer between writes.
//
// Platform notes:
// - Linux/macOS: kernel PTY buffer is typically 4KB; 256-byte chunks with 5ms delay works well.
// - Windows (conpty): has a smaller input buffer and cmd.exe/PowerShell process input slower,
//   so we use smaller chunks (128 bytes) with a longer delay (10ms) to stay safe.
const PTY_WRITE_CHUNK_SIZE = os.platform() === 'win32' ? 128 : 256;
const PTY_WRITE_CHUNK_DELAY_MS = os.platform() === 'win32' ? 10 : 5;

function writeToPtyChunked(ptyProcess: PtyProcess, data: string): void {
    if (data.length <= PTY_WRITE_CHUNK_SIZE) {
        ptyProcess.write(data);
        return;
    }

    let offset = 0;
    const writeNextChunk = () => {
        if (offset >= data.length) return;
        const chunk = data.slice(offset, offset + PTY_WRITE_CHUNK_SIZE);
        offset += PTY_WRITE_CHUNK_SIZE;
        ptyProcess.write(chunk);
        if (offset < data.length) {
            setTimeout(writeNextChunk, PTY_WRITE_CHUNK_DELAY_MS);
        }
    };
    writeNextChunk();
}

const MAX_COMMAND_RECORDS = 200;

function nowIso(): string {

                            type: "stepStarted",
                            threadId: finalThread.threadId,
                            stepId: step.stepId,
                            stepMessage: params.userMessage,
                            status: 'in_progress'
                        },
                        threadId: finalThread.threadId
                    });

                    // User message already sent before remote/local branch (lines 1038-1055)

                    // Process the message with agent
                    logger.info(`[CreateAndStartThread] Processing message with agent for thread ${finalThread.threadId}`);

                    // If taskId is provided, update the action plan item status
                    // if (params.taskId) {

                    //         logger.error(`[CreateAndStartThread] Failed to update action plan task status: ${error.message}`);
                    //     }
                    // }

                    // Send AgentProcessStarted event to parent WebSocket if provided and thread started successfully
                    if (ws) {
                        const agentProcessStartedEvent = {
                            type: 'ThreadAgentStarted',
                            threadId: createdThread.threadId,
                            agentId: messageObject.message?.selectedAgent?.id,
                            groupId: messageObject.message.groupId,
                            timestamp: new Date().toISOString()
                        };
                        try {
                            ws.send(JSON.stringify(agentProcessStartedEvent));
                            logger.info(`[ThreadServiceCLI] Sent AgentProcessStarted event to parent WS for thread ${createdThread.threadId}`);
                        } catch (error) {
                            logger.error(`[ThreadServiceCLI] Failed to send AgentProcessStarted event to parent WS: ${error}`);
                        }
                    }

                    // Now start processing the agent message
                    await processAgentMessage(messageObject as any, finalThread.threadId);
                    completionRecord.targetAgentInstanceId = resolveThreadAgentInstanceId(finalThread.threadId, completionRecord.targetAgentId);

                    logger.info(`[CreateAndStartThread] Thread ${finalThread.threadId} started`);
                    if (params.waitForCompletion) {
                        const completion = await waitForRegisteredThreadCompletion(finalThread.threadId);
                        return formatThreadCompletionResponse(completionRecord, completion);
                    }
                    return formatThreadStartedResponse(completionRecord);

                } catch (messageError: any) {
                    logger.error(`[CreateAndStartThread] Error processing message: ${messageError.message}`);
                    // Clean up the pending completion since we won't be waiting
                    pendingThreadCompletions.delete(finalThread.threadId);
                    // Return failure — thread was created but the agent failed to start
                    return {
                        success: false,
                        error: `Agent failed to start: ${messageError.message}`,
                        data: {
                            thread: finalThread as any,
                            activityId: 'activity-' + finalThread.threadId,
                            created: true,
                        }
                    };
                }
            }
            // No userMessage provided - return immediately without waiting for completion
            if (startedThread) {
                completionRecord.thread = startedThread;
                return formatThreadStartedResponse(completionRecord, 'IN_PROGRESS');
            } else {
                // Thread was created but failed to start - return the created thread anyway
                return {
                    success: true,
                    data: {
                        thread: createdThread as any,
                        activityId: 'activity-' + createdThread.threadId,
                        created: true
                    },
                    error: 'Thread created but failed to start'
                };
            }

        } catch (error: any) {
            const errorString = `Error creating and starting thread: ${error.message || JSON.stringify(error)}`;
            return {
                success: false,
                error: errorString

+const DEFAULT_THREAD_FOREGROUND_WAIT_MS = 5 * 60 * 1000;
+const DEFAULT_THREAD_AUTO_YIELD_MS = 30 * 1000;
+
+function normalizeThreadExecutionMode(params: Partial<CreateAndStartThreadInput>): AsyncTaskExecutionMode {
+    const requestedMode = params.executionMode || params.execution_mode;
+    if (
+        requestedMode === 'foreground_scoped' ||
+        requestedMode === 'auto_scoped' ||
+        requestedMode === 'background_scoped' ||
+        requestedMode === 'background_detached'
+    ) {
+        return requestedMode;
+    }
+    if (params.lifetime === 'detached') {
+        return 'background_detached';
+    }
+    if (params.waitForCompletion) {
+        return 'foreground_scoped';
+    }
+    return 'background_scoped';
+}
+
+function shouldWaitForThreadMode(executionMode?: AsyncTaskExecutionMode): boolean {
+    return executionMode === 'foreground_scoped' || executionMode === 'auto_scoped';
+}
+
+function getThreadModeWaitMs(executionMode: AsyncTaskExecutionMode, params: Partial<CreateAndStartThreadInput>): number {
+    if (typeof params.timeoutMs === 'number' && Number.isFinite(params.timeoutMs) && params.timeoutMs >= 0) {
+        return params.timeoutMs;
+    }
+    if (executionMode === 'auto_scoped' && typeof params.yieldMs === 'number' && Number.isFinite(params.yieldMs) && params.yieldMs >= 0) {
+        return params.yieldMs;
+    }
+    return executionMode === 'foreground_scoped'
+        ? DEFAULT_THREAD_FOREGROUND_WAIT_MS
+        : DEFAULT_THREAD_AUTO_YIELD_MS;
+}
+
+async function formatThreadResponseForExecutionMode(
+    record: PendingThreadCompletion,
+    params: Partial<CreateAndStartThreadInput>,
+    status = 'IN_PROGRESS',
+    output?: string,
+): Promise<ThreadServiceResponse<CreateAndStartThreadResponseData>> {
+    const executionMode = record.executionMode || normalizeThreadExecutionMode(params);
+    if (!shouldWaitForThreadMode(executionMode)) {
+        return formatThreadStartedResponse(record, status, output);
+    }
+

+        record.threadId,
+        getThreadModeWaitMs(executionMode, params),

+    if (waitResult.completed) {
+        return formatThreadCompletionResponse(record, waitResult.completion);
+    }
+
+    asyncTaskRegistry.updateTask(`thread:${record.threadId}`, {
+        executionMode: 'background_scoped',
+        summary: `Thread is still running after ${executionMode} wait; converted to background_scoped.`,
+        metadata: {
+            yieldReason: executionMode === 'foreground_scoped' ? 'foreground_timeout' : 'yield_timeout',
+            waitError: waitResult.error,
+        },
+    });
+    record.executionMode = 'background_scoped';
+
+    return formatThreadStartedResponse(
+        record,
+        status,
+        [
+            output,

+            waitResult.error,
+        ].filter(Boolean).join('\n'),

import { z } from 'zod';

/**
 * Terminal Event Schemas for Agent-to-App Communication
 * Based on codeboltjs/src/modules/terminal.ts module operations
 */

// Base terminal message schema
export const terminalEventBaseSchema = z.object({
  type: z.string(),
  requestId: z.string(),
});

// Execute Command Event Schema
export const executeCommandEventSchema = terminalEventBaseSchema.extend({
  type: z.literal('executeCommand'),
  message: z.string(),
  returnEmptyStringOnSuccess: z.boolean().optional(),
  executionMode: z.enum(['auto', 'foreground', 'background']).optional(),
  yieldMs: z.number().optional(),
  timeoutMs: z.number().optional(),
  backgroundOnYield: z.boolean().optional(),
});

// Execute Command Run Until Error Event Schema
export const executeCommandRunUntilErrorEventSchema = terminalEventBaseSchema.extend({
  type: z.literal('executeCommandRunUntilError'),
  message: z.string(),
  executeInMain: z.boolean().optional(),
});

// Execute Command With Stream Event Schema
export const executeCommandWithStreamEventSchema = terminalEventBaseSchema.extend({
  type: z.literal('executeCommandWithStream'),
  message: z.string(),
  executeInMain: z.boolean().optional(),
});

// Send Interrupt To Terminal Event Schema
export const sendInterruptToTerminalEventSchema = terminalEventBaseSchema.extend({
  type: z.literal('sendInterruptToTerminal'),
});

const tuiEventTypes = [
  'tuiRun',
  'tuiAttach',
  'tuiOutput',
  'tuiScreen',
  'tuiType',
  'tuiWrite',
  'tuiPress',
  'tuiResize',
  'tuiSearch',
  'tuiRegion',
  'tuiCursor',
  'tuiWait',
  'tuiWheel',
  'tuiSessionsList',
  'tuiSessionsSwitch',
  'tuiKill',
  'tuiCleanup',
] as const;

export const tuiEventSchema = terminalEventBaseSchema.extend({
  type: z.enum(tuiEventTypes),
  params: z.record(z.any()).optional(),
});

export const terminalCommandManagementEventSchema = terminalEventBaseSchema.extend({
  type: z.enum([
    'terminalCommandsList',
    'terminalCommandStop',
    'terminalCommandOutput',
    'terminalCommandStatus',
    'terminalCommandWait'
  ]),
  params: z.record(z.any()).optional(),
});

// Union of all terminal event schemas
export const terminalEventSchema = z.union([
  executeCommandEventSchema,
  executeCommandRunUntilErrorEventSchema,
  executeCommandWithStreamEventSchema,
  sendInterruptToTerminalEventSchema,
  tuiEventSchema,
  terminalCommandManagementEventSchema,
]);

// Execute Command Options Schema (for CLI service usage)
export const ExecuteCommandOptionsSchema = z.object({
  command: z.string(),
  returnEmptyStringOnSuccess: z.boolean().optional(),
  executeInMain: z.boolean().optional(),
  executionMode: z.enum(['auto', 'foreground', 'background']).optional(),
  execution_mode: z.enum(['auto', 'foreground', 'background']).optional(),
  yieldMs: z.number().optional(),
  yield_ms: z.number().optional(),
  timeoutMs: z.number().optional(),
  timeout_ms: z.number().optional(),
  backgroundOnYield: z.boolean().optional(),
  background_on_yield: z.boolean().optional(),
});

// Inferred TypeScript types for events
export type TerminalEventBase = z.infer<typeof terminalEventBaseSchema>;
export type ExecuteCommandEvent = z.infer<typeof executeCommandEventSchema>;
export type ExecuteCommandRunUntilErrorEvent = z.infer<typeof executeCommandRunUntilErrorEventSchema>;
export type ExecuteCommandWithStreamEvent = z.infer<typeof executeCommandWithStreamEventSchema>;
export type SendInterruptToTerminalEvent = z.infer<typeof sendInterruptToTerminalEventSchema>;
export type TuiEvent = z.infer<typeof tuiEventSchema>;
export type TerminalEvent = z.infer<typeof terminalEventSchema>;
export type ExecuteCommandOptions = z.infer<typeof ExecuteCommandOptionsSchema>;
]]></tool_result>

+<body>
+  <header>
+    <div class="inner">
+      <h1>Unified Async Task Execution Mode</h1>
+      <p class="subtitle">
+        This document explains the updated async task lifecycle implementation. Commands, child
+        threads, and future async process types now share one execution-mode vocabulary instead of
+        separate lifetime/task-kind fields.
+      </p>
+    </div>
+  </header>
+
+  <main>
+    <section>
+      <h2>Current Model</h2>
+      <p>
+        The public and registry-level model now has one main control field:
+        <code>executionMode</code>. It combines how long the runtime waits inline and whether the task
+        is scoped to the current agent run or intentionally detached.
+      </p>
+      <pre><code>status:
+  "running" | "completed" | "failed" | "stopped"
+
+executionMode:
+  "foreground_scoped"
+  "auto_scoped"
+  "background_scoped"
+  "background_detached"</code></pre>
+      <div class="callout">
+        <p>
+          <code>detached</code> is not a status and <code>task_kind</code> is no longer part of the
+          public command/thread tool surface. Long-running behavior is inferred from the execution
+          mode and runtime observations.
+        </p>
+      </div>
+    </section>
+
+    <section>
+      <h2>Execution Modes</h2>
+      <table>
+        <thead>
+          <tr>
+            <th>Mode</th>
+            <th>Inline behavior</th>
+            <th>If still running</th>
+            <th>User force-stop behavior</th>
+          </tr>
+        </thead>
+        <tbody>
+          <tr>
+            <td><code>foreground_scoped</code></td>
+            <td>Wait inline for a longer bounded foreground wait.</td>
+            <td>Convert to <code>background_scoped</code>, return task id and logs/status so far.</td>
+            <td>Stopped by runtime.</td>
+          </tr>
+          <tr>
+            <td><code>auto_scoped</code></td>
+            <td>Wait inline for a shorter yield window.</td>
+            <td>Convert to <code>background_scoped</code>, return task id and logs/status so far.</td>
+            <td>Stopped by runtime.</td>
+          </tr>
+          <tr>
+            <td><code>background_scoped</code></td>
+            <td>Return task id quickly.</td>
+            <td>Already running in background, but still owned by this agent run.</td>
+            <td>Stopped by runtime.</td>
+          </tr>
+          <tr>
+            <td><code>background_detached</code></td>
+            <td>Return task id quickly.</td>
+            <td>Runs as intentional background work.</td>
+            <td>Survives and is shown to the next agent process.</td>
+          </tr>
+        </tbody>
+      </table>
+    </section>
+
+    <section>
+      <h2>Files Changed</h2>
+      <ul class="files">
+        <li>packages/server/src/cliLib/asyncTaskRegistry.cli.ts</li>
+        <li>packages/server/src/cliLib/asyncTaskService.cli.ts</li>

+        <li>packages/server/src/cliLib/messageService.cli.ts</li>

+        <li>packages/types/src/wstypes/agent-to-app-ws/actions/threadEventSchemas.ts</li>

+    </section>
+
+    <section>
+      <h2>Async Task Registry</h2>
+      <p>
+        <code>asyncTaskRegistry.cli.ts</code> now stores each task with one unified
+        <code>executionMode</code>. A task record includes task id, type, status, execution mode,
+        owner thread, owner agent, owner agent instance, timestamps, title, summary, and metadata.
+      </p>
+      <p>
+        Detaching a task now means updating <code>executionMode</code> to
+        <code>background_detached</code>. Final task states remain only
+        <code>completed</code>, <code>failed</code>, and <code>stopped</code>.
+      </p>
+      <pre><code>async_task_control action="detach"
+  -> asyncTaskRegistry.detachTask(taskId)
+  -> executionMode = "background_detached"
+  -> status stays "running" until the task exits or is stopped</code></pre>
+    </section>
+
+    <section>
+      <h2>Command Behavior</h2>
+      <p>
+        <code>aiTerminal.ts</code> now normalizes command execution into the same four modes. Older
+        inputs like <code>foreground</code>, <code>auto</code>, <code>background</code>, and
+        <code>lifetime=detached</code> are still parsed for compatibility, but exposed schemas and
+        stored task records use the new enum.
+      </p>
+      <div class="flow">
+        <div class="step">
+          <strong>Start</strong>
+          <span>Register <code>command:&lt;pid&gt;</code> with the normalized execution mode.</span>
+        </div>
+        <div class="step">
+          <strong>Foreground timeout</strong>
+          <span>
+            <code>foreground_scoped</code> waits inline up to <code>timeout_ms</code> or the runtime
+            default. If still running, it becomes <code>background_scoped</code>.
+          </span>
+        </div>
+        <div class="step">
+          <strong>Auto yield</strong>
+          <span>
+            <code>auto_scoped</code> waits for <code>yield_ms</code> or the runtime default, then
+            becomes <code>background_scoped</code> if still running.
+          </span>
+        </div>
+        <div class="step">
+          <strong>No LLM status guess</strong>
+          <span>
+            The previous LLM-backed passed/failed/processing analysis is no longer used for lifecycle
+            timeout conversion. If the process is still running, it is running.
+          </span>
+        </div>
+      </div>
+      <pre><code>{
+  "command": "npm run build",
+  "execution_mode": "auto_scoped",
+  "yield_ms": 3000
+}</code></pre>
+      <pre><code>{
+  "command": "npm run dev",
+  "execution_mode": "background_detached"
+}</code></pre>
+    </section>
+
+    <section>
+      <h2>Child Thread Behavior</h2>
+      <p>
+        Child threads now use the same execution modes as commands. This means a child thread can be
+        started in <code>foreground_scoped</code>, <code>auto_scoped</code>,
+        <code>background_scoped</code>, or <code>background_detached</code>.
+      </p>
+      <table>
+        <thead>
+          <tr>
+            <th>Child thread mode</th>
+            <th>Behavior</th>
+          </tr>
+        </thead>
+        <tbody>
+          <tr>
+            <td><code>foreground_scoped</code></td>
+            <td>Start the child and wait boundedly for completion. If it does not finish, convert to <code>background_scoped</code>.</td>
+          </tr>
+          <tr>
+            <td><code>auto_scoped</code></td>
+            <td>Start the child and wait briefly. If it does not finish, return <code>thread:&lt;threadId&gt;</code>.</td>
+          </tr>
+          <tr>
+            <td><code>background_scoped</code></td>
+            <td>Return <code>thread:&lt;threadId&gt;</code> quickly. The parent run owns cleanup.</td>
+          </tr>
+          <tr>
+            <td><code>background_detached</code></td>
+            <td>Return <code>thread:&lt;threadId&gt;</code> quickly. The child survives parent/user force-stop.</td>
+          </tr>
+        </tbody>
+      </table>
+      <p>
+        <code>waitForCompletion</code> remains as a compatibility path and maps to
+        <code>foreground_scoped</code> when no explicit execution mode is provided.
+      </p>
+    </section>
+
+    <section>
+      <h2>Agent Perspective</h2>
+      <div class="grid">
+        <div class="card">
+          <h3><span class="tag">On Start</span>Context Injection</h3>
+          <p>
+            The agent receives the async task policy and current task state. Scoped tasks appear in
+            <code>&lt;pending_async_tasks&gt;</code>. Detached tasks appear in
+            <code>&lt;detached_async_tasks&gt;</code>.
+          </p>
+        </div>
+        <div class="card">
+          <h3><span class="tag">Before Completion</span>Exit Gate</h3>
+          <p>
+            <code>ResponseExecutor</code> checks current-run tasks. If any non-final task is not
+            <code>background_detached</code>, completion is rejected and the agent must wait, stop,
+            or detach it.
+          </p>
+        </div>
+      </div>
+      <h3>User Force-Stop</h3>
+      <p>
+        On force-stop, the runtime immediately stops active scoped tasks owned by the agent run.
+        <code>background_detached</code> tasks survive and are surfaced to the next agent process.
+      </p>
+      <pre><code>User stops agent
+  -> stop foreground_scoped / auto_scoped / background_scoped tasks owned by the run
+  -> leave background_detached tasks running
+  -> write observability metadata
+  -> next agent sees detached tasks in context</code></pre>
+    </section>
+
+    <section>
+      <h2>Task Control Tool</h2>
+      <p>
+        The canonical control surface is <code>async_task_control</code>:
+      </p>
+      <table>
+        <thead>
+          <tr>
+            <th>Action</th>
+            <th>Effect</th>
+          </tr>
+        </thead>
+        <tbody>
+          <tr>
+            <td><code>wait</code></td>
+            <td>Wait boundedly for a task. If the wait times out, the task stays running.</td>
+          </tr>
+          <tr>
+            <td><code>stop</code></td>
+            <td>Terminate the command or child thread and mark it <code>stopped</code>.</td>
+          </tr>
+          <tr>
+            <td><code>detach</code></td>
+            <td>Change <code>executionMode</code> to <code>background_detached</code>.</td>
+          </tr>
+        </tbody>
+      </table>
+    </section>
+
+    <section>
+      <h2>Examples</h2>
+      <div class="grid">
+        <div class="card">
+          <h3>Quick command</h3>
+          <pre><code>{
+  "command": "dir",
+  "execution_mode": "foreground_scoped"
+}</code></pre>
+          <p>If it finishes quickly, output returns inline. If not, it becomes <code>background_scoped</code>.</p>
+        </div>
+        <div class="card">
+          <h3>Build command</h3>
+          <pre><code>{
+  "command": "npm run build",
+  "execution_mode": "auto_scoped",
+  "yield_ms": 3000
+}</code></pre>
+          <p>The agent gets a task id if the build is still running after the yield window.</p>
+        </div>
+        <div class="card">
+          <h3>Dev server</h3>
+          <pre><code>{
+  "command": "npm run dev",
+  "execution_mode": "background_detached"
+}</code></pre>
+          <p>The dev server intentionally survives agent stop and completion.</p>
+        </div>
+        <div class="card">
+          <h3>Child thread</h3>
+          <pre><code>{
+  "task": "Analyze this module",
+  "selectedAgent": "worker-agent",
+  "execution_mode": "auto_scoped",
+  "yield_ms": 30000
+}</code></pre>
+          <p>The parent waits briefly, then continues with <code>thread:&lt;threadId&gt;</code> if needed.</p>
+        </div>
+      </div>
+    </section>
+
+    <section>
+      <h2>Validation Notes</h2>
+      <ul>
+        <li><code>npm run build --workspace=packages/server</code> passed.</li>
+        <li><code>npx tsc --noEmit --project packages/types/tsconfig.json</code> passed.</li>
+        <li>
+          SDK package builds still have pre-existing cross-package type drift, including missing
+          exported tool/LLM types. Those failures are separate from the server/runtime validation.
+        </li>
+      </ul>
+    </section>
+  </main>
+</body>
+</html>
*** End Patch

]]></arguments>
</tool_call>

<message role="assistant" ordinal="578" timestamp="2026-07-07T07:37:18.574Z">
Implemented the generalized common model.

What changed:
- Replaced separate public `lifetime` / `task_kind` model with one common `executionMode` enum:
  - `foreground_scoped`
  - `auto_scoped`
  - `background_scoped`
  - `background_detached`
- Async task registry now stores that same `executionMode`.
- `detach` now means: set `executionMode = &#34;background_detached&#34;`.
- Force-stop cleanup now stops every non-`background_detached` task owned by the run.
- Agent completion gate now blocks unresolved scoped tasks and ignores `background_detached`.

Command behavior:
- `foreground_scoped` waits inline up to `timeout_ms` or runtime default.
- If still running, it converts to `background_scoped` and returns `command:&lt;pid&gt;` plus logs so far.
- `auto_scoped` waits for `yield_ms`, then converts to `background_scoped`.
- Removed LLM command-status analysis from this lifecycle path.

Child thread behavior:
- Child threads now also support all four modes.
- `foreground_scoped` / `auto_scoped` wait boundedly, then convert to `background_scoped` if still running.
- `background_detached` survives force-stop.
- `waitForCompletion` is kept only as compatibility and maps to `foreground_scoped` if no explicit mode is given.

Updated the explainer HTML too:
[async-task-lifecycle-explainer.html](D:/codeboltapps/Codebolt/async-task-lifecycle-explainer.html)

Validation:
- `npm run build --workspace=packages/server` passed.
- `npx tsc --noEmit --project packages/types/tsconfig.json` passed.
- SDK builds still fail on existing cross-package type drift, not this runtime path.
</message>

        {/* Main Content */}
        <div>
          {/* Command display - stateEvent-based confirmation (new flow) */}
          {stateEvent === CommandConfirmationStateEnum.ASK_FOR_CONFIRMATION &&
            hasCommand && (
              <div

                  backgroundColor: 'var(--theme-sideBarBackground)',

                      >
                        <X className="mr-0.5 h-3 w-3" />

                      </Button>
                      <Button
                        size="xss"
                        className="h-5 px-1.5 text-[10px]"
                        onClick={handleApproveCommand}
                      >
                        <CheckCheck className="mr-0.5 h-3 w-3" />
                        Run
                      </Button>
                    </div>
                  </div>
                </div>
              </div>
            )}

          {/* Command display - Legacy ConfirmationRequest flow */}
          {stateEvent !== CommandConfirmationStateEnum.ASK_FOR_CONFIRMATION &&
            data.actionType === TemplateEnum.ConfirmationRequest &&

              <div
                className="mb-2 rounded overflow-hidden"
                style={{
                  backgroundColor: 'var(--theme-sideBarBackground)',

                {/* Command Header */}
                <div
                  className="px-3 py-1.5"

                >
                  <div className="flex items-center justify-between">

                      <span
                        className="font-medium text-[11px]"

                    {data.actionType === TemplateEnum.ConfirmationRequest &&

                          <span className="opacity-70">⌃⏎</span>

                        </div>
                      )}
                  </div>
                </div>
                {/* Command Content */}
                <div className="px-3 pt-2 pb-2.5">
                  <div className="flex items-start gap-1.5 font-mono text-[11px] leading-relaxed">
                    <span className="select-none" style={{ color: 'var(--theme-textSeparator)' }}>
                      $
                    </span>
                    <span
                      className="break-all"
                      style={{ color: 'var(--theme-foreground)' }}
                    >
                      {command}

                  </div>
                  <div className="mt-2 flex items-center justify-between text-[10px]" style={{ color: 'var(--theme-textSeparator)' }}>

                    {data.actionType === TemplateEnum.ConfirmationRequest &&

                          >
                            <X className="mr-0.5 h-3 w-3" />
                            Cancel
                          </Button>
                          <Button
                            size="xss"
                            className="h-5 px-1.5 text-[10px]"
                            onClick={() => {
                              const acceptButton = data?.data?.buttons.find(

                              if (acceptButton) handleButtonnClick(acceptButton);

                      )}

          {confirmationState !== TerminalProcessStatus.idle &&

                style={{
                  backgroundColor: 'transparent',
                  border: '1px solid var(--theme-panelBorder)',

              >

                    <Button

                  </ErrorBoundary>
                )}
              </div>
            )}
        </div>

        {/* Footer */}
        <div className="pt-2">
          <div className="w-full space-y-2">
            {/* Action buttons based on state */}
            {!isHistoricalMessage && (
              <>

                {/* Status indicator while LLM analyzes stopped command */}
                {(confirmationState === TerminalProcessStatus.Stopping ||
                  confirmationState === TerminalProcessStatus.Stopped) &&
                  !isExternalStop && (
                    <div
                      className="flex flex-col gap-2 p-3 rounded"
                      style={{
                        backgroundColor: 'var(--theme-sideBarBackground)',
                        border: '1px solid var(--theme-panelBorder)',
                      }}
                    >
                      <div className="flex items-center gap-2">
                        <span
                          className="animate-ping h-2 w-2 rounded-full inline-block"
                          style={{ backgroundColor: 'var(--theme-terminalAnsiYellow)' }}
                        />
                        <p
                          className="text-xs font-medium"
                          style={{ color: 'var(--theme-textSeparator)' }}
                        >
                          Analyzing command result...
                        </p>
                      </div>
                    </div>
                  )}

                {/* Long running process options */}
                {confirmationState ===
                  TerminalProcessStatus.LongRunningProcessStarted && (
                    <div
                      className="flex flex-col gap-2 p-3 rounded"
                      style={{
                        backgroundColor: 'var(--theme-sideBarBackground)',
                        border: '1px solid var(--theme-panelBorder)',
                      }}
                    >
                      <p
                        className="text-xs font-medium"
                        style={{ color: 'var(--theme-textSeparator)' }}
                      >
                        {isYieldPending
                          ? 'Command is still running. It will continue automatically unless you act now.'
                          : 'Server detected. How would you like to proceed?'}
                      </p>
                      {!selectedButton ? (
                        <div className="flex flex-wrap gap-2">
                          {!isYieldPending && (
                            <Button
                              size="xss"
                              variant="outline"
                              onClick={() => handleExecutingButtonsClick('noclose')}
                              className="h-6 px-3 text-xs"
                            >
                              Keep Open
                            </Button>
                          )}
                          <Button
                            size="xss"
                            onClick={() =>
                              handleExecutingButtonsClick('runinbackground')
                            }
                            className="h-6 px-3 text-xs"
                          >
                            {isYieldPending ? 'Run in Background Now' : 'Run in Background'}
                          </Button>
                          <Button
                            size="xss"
                            variant="outline"
                            onClick={() =>
                              handleExecutingButtonsClick(isYieldPending ? 'noclose' : 'commandfailed')
                            }
                            className="h-6 px-3 text-xs"
                          >
                            {isYieldPending ? 'Stop Command' : 'Command Failed'}
                          </Button>
                        </div>
                      ) : (
                        <Button
                          disabled
                          size="xss"
                          className="h-6 px-3 text-xs capitalize w-fit"
                        >
                          {selectedButton === 'runinbackground'
                            ? 'Running in Background'
                            : selectedButton === 'noclose'
                              ? (isYieldPending ? 'Stopping Command' : 'Kept Open')
                              : 'Command Failed'}
                        </Button>
                      )}
                    </div>
                  )}
              </>
            )}

            {/* Status messages for accepted/denied states */}
            {(stateEvent === CommandConfirmationStateEnum.REJECTED ||
              confirmationState === TerminalProcessStatus.Denied) && (
                <div className="flex items-center gap-2 text-xs" style={{ color: 'var(--theme-terminalAnsiRed, #f87171)' }}>
                  <X className="h-3 w-3" />
                  <span>Command rejected</span>
                </div>
              )}
            {(stateEvent === CommandConfirmationStateEnum.ACCEPTED ||
              confirmationState === TerminalProcessStatus.Accepted) &&
              stateEvent !== CommandConfirmationStateEnum.REJECTED &&
              confirmationState !== TerminalProcessStatus.Denied && (
                <div className="flex items-center gap-2 text-xs" style={{ color: 'var(--theme-textSeparator)' }}>
                  <CheckCheck className="h-3 w-3" />
                  <span>Command accepted</span>
                </div>
              )}
          </div>
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>
  );
};

export default CommandConfirmation;

import { ArrowRight, CheckCheck, SquareTerminal, X } from 'lucide-react';
import React, { useEffect, useState } from 'react';
import { Button } from '../../../../ui-components/button';
import { TerminalProcessStatus } from '@/src/types/commandTypes';
import useInputStore from '../../../../Store/InputDataStore/InputDataStore';
import aiShellsocketStore from '../../../../Store/AIShellComponentStore/AIShellComponent';
import { ChatComponentEventEmitter } from '../../../../Events/ChatComponentEventEmitter';
import { ChatEventEmitter } from '../../../../Events/ChatEventEmitter';
import { TemplateEnum, CommandConfirmationStateEnum } from '@/src/types/chatTypes';
import useInputStateMainStore, {
  InputMainStates,
} from '../../../../Store/InputDataStore/InputMainStore';
import { AIShellComponent } from '../../../../Pages/Panels/AIShellPanel/AIShellComponent';

const isDev = false; // process.env.NODE_ENV === 'development';
// Simple error boundary to catch terminal errors
class ErrorBoundary extends React.Component<{
  children: React.ReactNode;
  onError: (error: Error) => void;
}> {
  state = { hasError: false };

  static getDerivedStateFromError(error: Error) {
    return { hasError: true };
  }

  componentDidCatch(error: Error, errorInfo: React.ErrorInfo) {
    console.error('Terminal error:', error, errorInfo);
    this.props.onError(error);
  }

  render() {
    if (this.state.hasError) {
      return null; // Parent will handle the error UI
    }

    return this.props.children;
  }
}

const CommandConfirmation = ({ data }) => {
  const { terminalID, setTerminalID } = aiShellsocketStore();
  const [selectedButton, setSelectedButton] = useState(null);
  const [selectedYesNoButton, setSelectedYesNoButton] = useState(null);
  // Check if this is a historical message or active command
  const isHistoricalMessage =
    data.historyType === 'historical' ||
    data.templateType === TemplateEnum.COMMANDCONFIRMATIONHISTORY;

  // Historical messages don't have a live terminal, so default to false
  // to show the static command display instead
  const [showInlineTerminal, setShowInlineTerminal] = useState(!isHistoricalMessage);
  const [terminalError, setTerminalError] = useState(false);
  const [terminalHeight, setTerminalHeight] = useState('200px');

  // Get current processing state from the store
  const { processMainState } = useInputStateMainStore();
  const isAgentProcessing = processMainState === InputMainStates.PROCESSING;

  // Track if the process was stopped externally to avoid showing confirmation
  const [isExternalStop, setIsExternalStop] = useState(false);

  // Extract initial processId and command more reliably
  const initialProcessId =
    data?.payload?.processId ||
    data?.data?.text?.payload?.processId ||
    (data?.messageHistory?.length > 0
      ? data.messageHistory[data.messageHistory.length - 1].payload?.processId
      : null);

  const [processId, setProcessId] = useState(initialProcessId);

  const command =
    data?.payload?.command ||
    data?.data?.text?.payload?.command ||
    (data?.messageHistory?.length > 0
      ? data.messageHistory[data.messageHistory.length - 1].payload?.command
      : null);

  // Track stateEvent from payload (askForConfirmation, accepted, rejected)
  const initialStateEvent =
    data?.payload?.stateEvent ||
    data?.data?.text?.payload?.stateEvent ||
    (data?.messageHistory?.length > 0
      ? data.messageHistory[data.messageHistory.length - 1].payload?.stateEvent
      : null);

  const [stateEvent, setStateEvent] = useState(initialStateEvent);
  const isYieldPending =
    data?.payload?.yieldPending ||
    data?.data?.text?.payload?.yieldPending ||
    (data?.messageHistory?.length > 0
      ? data.messageHistory[data.messageHistory.length - 1].payload?.yieldPending
      : false);

  // Initialize confirmation state based on message type
  const [confirmationState, setConfirmationState] = useState(
    // For historical messages
    isHistoricalMessage
      ? data.messageHistory?.length > 0
        ? data.messageHistory[data.messageHistory.length - 1].payload?.status ||
        TerminalProcessStatus.Done
        : TerminalProcessStatus.Done
      : // For active commands
      data.messageHistory?.length > 0
        ? data.messageHistory[data.messageHistory.length - 1].payload.status
        : (data?.data?.text?.payload?.status ?? TerminalProcessStatus.idle),
  );

  // Set the terminal ID from data when component mounts and handle auto-execution
  useEffect(() => {
    if (isDev) console.log(
      `CommandConfirmation: processId=${processId}, command=${command}, templateType=${data.templateType}`,
    );

    // Historical messages don't need terminal setup — they only show static command display
    if (isHistoricalMessage) return;

    // If this is not a confirmation template, set status to Executing immediately
    if (data.templateType !== TemplateEnum.COMMANDCONFIRMATION && processId) {
      if (isDev) console.log('Auto-executing command without confirmation');
      setConfirmationState(TerminalProcessStatus.Executing);
    }

    // If this component has a process ID and we don't have a terminal ID set yet or it's different
    if (processId && (!terminalID || terminalID.id !== processId)) {
      if (isDev) console.log(`Setting terminalID to: ${processId} (${command})`);
      setTerminalID({
        id: processId,
        processName: command,
      });
      // Always show terminal by default
      setShowInlineTerminal(true);
    }
    // Also show terminal by default if we already have a terminal ID
    else if (processId) {
      setShowInlineTerminal(true);
    }
  }, [processId, command]);

  // Recalculate terminal height based on command output
  useEffect(() => {
    if (showInlineTerminal) {
      // Default height based on expected content - increased from 120px to 160px
      let calculatedHeight = 160;

      // Increase height for longer commands or if we're showing a server process - increased from 150px to 200px
      if (
        command &&
        (command.length > 80 ||
          command.includes('npm') ||
          command.includes('start') ||
          command.includes('server'))
      ) {
        calculatedHeight = 200;
      }

      // Set a maximum height based on viewport - increased from 300px to 400px and 30% to 40%
      const maxHeight = Math.min(400, window.innerHeight * 0.4);
      setTerminalHeight(`${Math.min(calculatedHeight, maxHeight)}px`);
    }
  }, [showInlineTerminal, command]);

  const handleButtonnClick = (value) => {
    if (value.buttonClickedText === 'Accept') {
      setConfirmationState(TerminalProcessStatus.Accepted);

      // When accepted, set the terminal ID and show inline terminal
      if (processId) {
        if (isDev) console.log(`Accept clicked: Setting terminalID to ${processId}`);
        setTerminalID({
          id: processId,
          processName: command,
        });
        // Keep terminal visible
        setShowInlineTerminal(true);
      }
    }
    if (value.buttonClickedText === 'Reject') {
      setConfirmationState(TerminalProcessStatus.Denied);
    }
    const inputJson = useInputStore.getState().inputJson;
    const messagePayload = {
      type: 'confirmationResponse',
      message: {
        ...inputJson,
        messageId: data.messageId,
        threadId: data.threadId,
        userMessage: value.value,
        templateType: TemplateEnum.COMMANDCONFIRMATION,
        // Include agent properties for history tracking
        agentInstanceId: data.agentInstanceId,
        agentId: data.agentId,
        parentAgentInstanceId: data.parentAgentInstanceId,
        parentId: data.parentId,
      },
      agentInstanceId: data.agentInstanceId,
      agentId: data.agentId,
      parentAgentInstanceId: data.parentAgentInstanceId,
      parentId: data.parentId,
    };

    ChatEventEmitter.emit('SOCKET_CHAT_SEND', messagePayload);
  };

  // Handle approve via stateEvent-based confirmation (similar to WriteFileTemplate)
  const handleApproveCommand = () => {
    setStateEvent(CommandConfirmationStateEnum.ACCEPTED);
    setConfirmationState(TerminalProcessStatus.Accepted);

    if (processId) {
      setTerminalID({
        id: processId,
        processName: command,
      });
      setShowInlineTerminal(true);
    }

    const inputJson = useInputStore.getState().inputJson;
    const messagePayload = {
      type: 'confirmationResponse',
      message: {
        ...inputJson,
        messageId: data.messageId,
        threadId: data.threadId,
        userMessage: 'Approve',
        type: 'confirmationResponse',
        action: 'approve',
        templateType: TemplateEnum.COMMANDCONFIRMATION,
        // Include agent properties for history tracking
        agentInstanceId: data.agentInstanceId,
        agentId: data.agentId,
        parentAgentInstanceId: data.parentAgentInstanceId,
        parentId: data.parentId,
      },
      agentInstanceId: data.agentInstanceId,
      agentId: data.agentId,
      parentAgentInstanceId: data.parentAgentInstanceId,
      parentId: data.parentId,
    };
    ChatEventEmitter.emit('SOCKET_CHAT_SEND', messagePayload);
  };

  // Handle reject via stateEvent-based confirmation (similar to WriteFileTemplate)
  const handleRejectCommand = () => {
    setStateEvent(CommandConfirmationStateEnum.REJECTED);
    setConfirmationState(TerminalProcessStatus.Denied);

    const inputJson = useInputStore.getState().inputJson;
    const messagePayload = {
      type: 'confirmationResponse',
      message: {
        ...inputJson,
        messageId: data.messageId,
        threadId: data.threadId,
        userMessage: 'Reject',
        templateType: TemplateEnum.COMMANDCONFIRMATION,
        agentInstanceId: data.agentInstanceId,
        agentId: data.agentId,
        parentAgentInstanceId: data.parentAgentInstanceId,
        parentId: data.parentId,
      },
      agentInstanceId: data.agentInstanceId,
      agentId: data.agentId,
      parentAgentInstanceId: data.parentAgentInstanceId,
      parentId: data.parentId,
    };
    ChatEventEmitter.emit('SOCKET_CHAT_SEND', messagePayload);
  };

  useEffect(() => {
    const handleMainCommunication = (message) => {
      setConfirmationState(message.payload.status);

      // Update stateEvent if present in the message
      if (message.payload.stateEvent) {
        setStateEvent(message.payload.stateEvent);
      }

      if (isDev) console.log(
        `Received status update: ${message.payload.status}, stateEvent: ${message.payload.stateEvent}, processId: ${message.payload.processId}`,
      );

      // Update processId if it's available in the message
      const newProcessId = message.payload.processId;

      // Update the processId state when a real PID arrives
      if (newProcessId && newProcessId !== processId) {
        setProcessId(newProcessId);
      }

      // When the terminal process starts, show the inline terminal
      if (
        (message.payload.status === TerminalProcessStatus.Executing ||
          message.payload.status ===
          TerminalProcessStatus.LongRunningProcessStarted) &&
        newProcessId
      ) {
        if (isDev) console.log(`Process started: Setting terminalID to ${newProcessId}`);
        setTerminalID({
          id: newProcessId,
          processName: message.payload.command || command,
        });
        // Always show terminal when process starts
        setShowInlineTerminal(true);
      }
    };

    // Listen for updates specific to this message
    ChatComponentEventEmitter.on(data.messageId, handleMainCommunication);

    // Also listen for process-specific updates if we have a processId
    // This ensures we receive updates when the process is stopped from other components
    const handleProcessSpecificUpdate = (message) => {
      // Only handle updates for our specific process
      if (
        message.payload?.processId === processId ||
        message.processId === processId
      ) {
        if (isDev) console.log(
          `CommandConfirmation: Received process-specific update for processId ${processId}:`,
          message.payload?.status || message.status,
        );

        // Check if this is an external stop
        if (message.externalStop || message.payload?.externalStop) {
          if (isDev) console.log(
            `CommandConfirmation: Process ${processId} was stopped externally, bypassing confirmation`,
          );
          setIsExternalStop(true);
          handleStop();
          // Call handleStop to send the stop command through WebSocket
          // Only call if we're in an executing state
          if (confirmationState === TerminalProcessStatus.Executing ||
            confirmationState === TerminalProcessStatus.LongRunningProcessStarted) {
            // handleStop();
          }

          // Update the confirmation state to Done when externally stopped
          setConfirmationState(TerminalProcessStatus.Done);
        }

        // Update the confirmation state based on the message
        const newStatus = message.payload?.status || message.status;
        if (
          newStatus &&
          Object.values(TerminalProcessStatus).includes(newStatus)
        ) {
          setConfirmationState(newStatus);
        }

        // Always show terminal when we receive process updates
        if (processId) {
          setShowInlineTerminal(true);
        }
      }
    };

    if (processId) {
      // Listen for process-specific updates using the processId as the event key
      ChatComponentEventEmitter.on(
        `process-${processId}`,
        handleProcessSpecificUpdate,
      );

      // Also listen for general terminal process updates
      ChatComponentEventEmitter.on(
        'TERMINAL_PROCESS_UPDATE',
        handleProcessSpecificUpdate,
      );
    }

    // Cleanup event listeners on unmount
    return () => {
      ChatComponentEventEmitter.off(data.messageId, handleMainCommunication);
      if (processId) {
        ChatComponentEventEmitter.off(
          `process-${processId}`,
          handleProcessSpecificUpdate,
        );

<message role="assistant" ordinal="583" timestamp="2026-07-07T08:59:12.553Z">
It is stale UI copy from the older command flow.

In [CommandConfirmation.tsx](D:/codeboltapps/Codebolt/packages/ui/src/Components/ChatComponets/Templates/ConfirmationTemplate/CommandConfirmation.tsx:961), that text is shown when:
<code_block language="ts"><![CDATA[
confirmationState === TerminalProcessStatus.Stopping ||
confirmationState === TerminalProcessStatus.Stopped
]]></code_block>
and it says:
<code_block language="tsx"><![CDATA[
Analyzing command result...
]]></code_block>
That made sense in the old server behavior because `aiTerminal.ts` had an LLM-backed command analysis path: after timeout/stop it would ask LLM whether the command was `passed`, `failed`, or `processing`.

But after our latest change, that model is no longer correct:
- foreground timeout no longer asks LLM to analyze result
- still-running command converts to `background_scoped`
- stop means stop
- process exit code decides completed/failed

So this UI text is now misleading. It should probably become one of:
<code_block language="text"><![CDATA[
Stopping command...
]]></code_block>
or
<code_block language="text"><![CDATA[
Command is stopping...
]]></code_block>
And if the command has already stopped:
<code_block language="text"><![CDATA[
Command stopped
]]></code_block>
Also, the comment above it says:
<code_block language="tsx"><![CDATA[
{/* Status indicator while LLM analyzes stopped command */}
]]></code_block>
That comment is definitely outdated now.
</message>

Yes. We should update it.

Change that UI block from “Analyzing command result...” to state-based copy:

- `Stopping` -&gt; `Stopping command...`
- `Stopped` -&gt; `Command stopped`

Also update the comment from:
<code_block language="tsx"><![CDATA[
{/* Status indicator while LLM analyzes stopped command */}
]]></code_block>
to:
<code_block language="tsx"><![CDATA[
{/* Status indicator while command is stopping or stopped */}
]]></code_block>
This matches the new deterministic lifecycle model and removes the old LLM-analysis implication.

function formatOutputForFileApplication(output, command, exitCode) {
    // Create a structured output format that's easy to parse
    const formattedOutput = {
        command: command,
        status: exitCode === 0 ? "success" : "error",
        exitCode: exitCode,
        timestamp: new Date().toISOString(),
        output: output.trim()
    };

    return JSON.stringify(formattedOutput, null, 2);
}

export async function executeCommandInShell(command: string, terminalId: string | number, finalMessage, notifyUser): Promise<any> {
    return new Promise(async (resolve, reject) => {
        let activeMessageId = finalMessage.messageId;
        let threadId = finalMessage.threadId;
        let initialOpenPorts: number[] = [];

            : (executionOptions.yieldMs ?? DEFAULT_AUTO_YIELD_MS);

                reject(error);
            }

            if (commandCompleted) return;
            resolvedAsBackground = true;
            const backgroundExecutionMode = backgroundModeFor(executionOptions.executionMode);
            resetTerminalIdOnProcessFinish(terminalId);
            updateTerminalProcessStatus(ptyProcess.pid, 'background');
            updateManagedCommand(ptyProcess.pid, {
                yielded: true,
                yieldReason: reason,
                port,
                outputTail: buffer.slice(-64 * 1024),
            });
            asyncTaskRegistry.updateTask(`command:${ptyProcess.pid}`, {
                executionMode: backgroundExecutionMode,
                metadata: {
                    yieldReason: reason,
                    port,
                    outputTail: buffer.slice(-64 * 1024),
                },
            });

            const runningMessage = {
                eventType: 'console',
                type: 'command',
                message: `${command} is running in the background. View Logs.`,
                processId: ptyProcess.pid,
                command,
                status: TerminalProcessStatus.RunningInBackground,
                messageId: finalMessage.messageId,
                threadId,
                agentInstanceId: finalMessage.agentInstanceId,
                agentId: finalMessage.agentId,
                parentAgentInstanceId: finalMessage.parentAgentInstanceId,
                parentId: finalMessage.parentId,
                timestamp: new Date().toISOString(),
                port,
                reason,
            };

            if (notifyUser) updateProcessStateInUi(runningMessage);

            safeResolve({
                result: buffer || '',
                output: buffer || '',
                type: 'commandRunning',
                status: 'running',
                status_code: 0,
                processId: ptyProcess.pid,
                reason,
                port,
                executionMode: backgroundExecutionMode,
            });
        };

        // Validate command
        if (!command || command.trim() === '') {
            safeReject(new Error('Command cannot be empty'));
            return;

        // host bridge/native PTY load failures otherwise leave this Promise
        // pending forever when the async executor rejects.

        try {

        } catch (error) {
            safeReject(error);
            return;
        }
        registerManagedCommand(ptyProcess.pid, terminalId, command, finalMessage, executionOptions);

        // to avoid race condition where fast commands exit before handlers are attached.

        ptyProcess.on('error', (error) => {
            cLogger.log(FocusedLogCategory.TOOL_EXECUTION, 'error', {

                operation: 'execute',
                parameters: {},

                .replace(/\x1b\[\?[0-9;]*[a-zA-Z]/g, '')
                .replace(/\x1b\([A-Z]/g, '')
                .replace(/\x1b[>=]/g, '')
                .replace(/\r/g, '')
                .trim();
            if (buffer.length < MAX_BUFFER_SIZE) {
                buffer += data;
            } else if (buffer.length >= MAX_BUFFER_SIZE && !buffer.endsWith('[truncated]')) {
                buffer = buffer.slice(-MAX_BUFFER_SIZE / 2) + '\n[truncated]';
            }

        ptyProcess.onExit(async ({ exitCode: ptyExitCode, signal: ptySignal }) => {

            const existingCommandRecord = commandRecords.get(ptyProcess.pid);

                || command.includes(" >> ");
            const formattedResult = isFileCommand

                : cleanedBuffer;

            let exitMessage = {
                eventType: 'console',
                type: 'command',
                message: isPassed ? `${command} Finished View Logs.` : `${command} Failed View Logs.`,
                processId: ptyProcess.pid,
                command,
                status: terminalStatus,
                messageId: finalMessage.messageId,
                threadId,
                agentInstanceId: finalMessage.agentInstanceId,

                parentId: finalMessage.parentId,
                timestamp: new Date().toISOString(),
            }

            resetTerminalIdOnProcessFinish(terminalId);
            updateTerminalProcessStatus(ptyProcess.pid, isPassed ? 'done' : 'failed');
            finalizeManagedCommand(
